prompt: A manufacturer is starting a ransomware resilience programme with a limited first-year budget. The CISO asks which workstream Microsoft's ransomware guidance says to complete first so that an extortion attempt cannot force the company to pay. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy microsegmentation across every datacenter network
Roll out phishing-resistant MFA to every user account
Prepare a recovery plan with secured and tested backups
Remove legacy protocols from all servers and devices

explanation: Microsoft's guidance orders the work as: prepare a recovery plan, then limit the scope of damage, then make it harder to get in, because the ability to restore operations without paying removes the attacker's leverage. Microsegmentation, phishing-resistant MFA for all users and removing legacy protocols are valuable, but they belong to the later phases and should not delay secured, tested backups.

prompt: A company protects Azure VMs with a Recovery Services vault. A threat model shows that an attacker who compromises a Backup Contributor account could disable soft delete and reduce retention before encrypting the VMs. The design must require a second party, who has no rights on the vault, to authorise such operations. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Multi-user authorization with a Resource Guard owned by a separate team
A CanNotDelete resource lock applied to the Recovery Services vault and its resource group
Cross Region Restore enabled on a geo-redundant vault
Customer-managed keys for encryption of the backup data

explanation: Multi-user authorization places critical vault operations behind a Resource Guard that is owned by someone else, ideally in another subscription or tenant, so a compromised backup administrator cannot weaken protection alone. A CanNotDelete lock only stops deletion of the vault resource and does not gate changes to soft delete or retention. Cross Region Restore addresses regional outages, and customer-managed keys control encryption, neither of which adds a second authoriser.

prompt: A financial regulator requires that backup recovery points cannot be deleted or have their retention shortened before they expire, by anyone including the vault owner, and that this protection cannot later be switched off. Which Azure Backup configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Enhanced soft delete configured with the always-on state
Multi-user authorization protected by a Resource Guard
Geo-redundant storage selected for the Recovery Services vault
Vault immutability that is enabled and then locked

explanation: An immutable vault blocks operations that would remove recovery points or reduce their retention before expiry, and locking the setting makes it irreversible even for the vault owner. Always-on soft delete keeps deleted backup data recoverable for the soft delete period but does not stop retention from being reduced. Multi-user authorization still allows the operation once someone approves it, and geo-redundant storage only protects against regional loss.

prompt: An architect is asked to design a security strategy that supports the business resiliency goals of a hospital group. Security funding cannot cover every system equally. What should the architect do first?

options.text: Apply one uniform control baseline to every system in the estate, whatever its business role
Identify business-critical systems with their owners and rank threats by impact
Remediate every vulnerability with the highest CVSS score first
Model defences on the most recently publicised threat actor

explanation: A resiliency strategy starts by working with business owners to identify the systems and dependencies the organisation cannot operate without, then prioritising threats by their impact on those assets. A uniform baseline spreads limited funding without regard to criticality. Ranking purely by CVSS score or by the latest publicised threat actor ignores which assets actually matter to the business.

prompt: A retailer runs its order system on VMware and Hyper-V virtual machines in its own datacenter. The business requires a low recovery time objective, orchestrated failover to Azure in a defined order, and regular disaster recovery drills that do not affect production. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Backup using the MARS agent on each server
Azure Site Recovery with recovery plans and test failover
Azure Migrate with a one-time replication of each server
Azure Arc-enabled servers with Azure Monitor Agent

explanation: Azure Site Recovery continuously replicates on-premises machines to Azure, sequences failover with recovery plans and supports test failover into an isolated network without disrupting production. Azure Backup with the MARS agent restores data but does not provide orchestrated low-RTO failover. Azure Migrate is intended for one-way migration, and Azure Arc with Azure Monitor Agent provides management and monitoring, not replication.

prompt: An incident review finds that ransomware operators harvested a Domain Admin credential from a help desk workstation and used it to encrypt most servers within hours. Backups already meet the recovery objectives. Which recommendation best limits the scope of damage in a future attack?

options.text: Increase the backup frequency for all servers to hourly and keep an extra copy in a second region
Add Safe Links scanning to all inbound email messages
Place a web application firewall in front of public sites
Restrict privileged accounts to dedicated admin workstations and tiers

explanation: The second phase of Microsoft's ransomware guidance is to limit the scope of damage by protecting privileged access, so that high-privilege credentials are only used from dedicated privileged access workstations and are never exposed on lower-trust systems. More frequent backups improve recovery but do not stop a stolen credential from reaching every server. Safe Links and a web application firewall reduce initial entry and do not address credential theft and lateral movement.

prompt: A company has 600 Azure VMs, 300 on-premises Windows and Linux servers and a set of AWS EC2 instances. The architect must recommend a solution that gives one view of missing security updates and deploys them on defined schedules across all three locations. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Update Manager with non-Azure machines connected through Azure Arc
Windows Server Update Services deployed separately in each location with a shared approval process
Microsoft Intune update rings assigned to all server devices
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management remediation requests

explanation: Azure Update Manager assesses and schedules updates for Windows and Linux machines in Azure and, through Azure Arc-enabled servers, for on-premises and other-cloud machines from one place. Separate WSUS deployments cover only Windows and give no single view. Intune update rings target Windows client devices rather than servers, and Defender Vulnerability Management identifies and prioritises missing updates but does not itself schedule their deployment.

prompt: A company uses Azure Update Manager. Servers are created and retired daily, and every machine tagged Environment=Production must automatically join the monthly patch schedule without an administrator editing the list of machines. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Periodic assessment enabled on every subscription
Automatic VM guest patching enabled on each machine
A maintenance configuration that uses a dynamic scope
An Azure Policy assignment that uses the audit effect

explanation: A dynamic scope attached to a maintenance configuration selects machines at run time by criteria such as tags, so new production servers are patched on the schedule automatically. Periodic assessment only checks for missing updates every 24 hours. Automatic VM guest patching lets the platform choose the timing rather than the company schedule, and an audit policy reports non-compliance without scheduling anything.

prompt: Several vulnerabilities are being actively exploited, and the operations team can patch only a fraction of endpoints each week. The security architect must evaluate which solution best tells the team which weaknesses to fix first, based on exploit availability, threat context and device exposure. Which solution should be selected?

options.text: Azure Update Manager update compliance reports
Windows Autopatch quality update status reports
Azure Advisor security recommendations
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

explanation: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management prioritises weaknesses using threat intelligence, exploit availability and the exposure of affected devices, which supports risk-based patching. Azure Update Manager and Windows Autopatch reports show which updates are missing or installed but do not rank them by exploitation risk. Azure Advisor surfaces general Azure resource recommendations rather than endpoint vulnerability prioritisation.

prompt: A company manages 9,000 Windows 11 devices with Microsoft Intune. It wants quality updates deployed through progressive rings, with Microsoft operating the rollout and pausing it when problems are detected, so that the small endpoint team spends less time on patching. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Windows Autopatch
Azure Update Manager
Windows Server Update Services
Configuration Manager software update points

explanation: Windows Autopatch is a Microsoft-operated service that moves Intune-managed Windows devices through deployment rings and can pause a release when issues appear. Azure Update Manager is designed for servers in Azure and Arc-connected machines, not for client fleets. WSUS and Configuration Manager software update points require the team to run infrastructure and approve and stage updates themselves, which increases rather than reduces effort.

prompt: A company stores its backups on a domain-joined file server that the same administrators manage as production. The architect must specify a backup requirement that keeps recovery possible after a human-operated ransomware attack that gains Domain Admin rights. Which requirement should be specified?

options.text: Replicate the backup share to a second domain-joined file server
Keep immutable or offline copies and test restores on a schedule
Take volume shadow copies on the backup server every hour
Compress and encrypt backup files with a key held on the server

explanation: Human-operated ransomware deliberately destroys reachable backups, so copies must be immutable or offline and restores must be rehearsed to prove recovery works. A replica on another domain-joined server and hourly shadow copies remain under the control of the same compromised administrators and can be deleted or encrypted. Encrypting backups with a key on the same server protects confidentiality but not availability.

prompt: An application writes business-critical documents to block blobs in an Azure Storage account. The design must allow the containers to be returned to their state at a chosen earlier time after a malicious mass overwrite or deletion. Which configuration should the architect recommend?

options.text: Geo-zone-redundant storage with read access to the secondary
Customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault
Point-in-time restore with versioning and soft delete
A lifecycle management policy that tiers blobs to archive

explanation: Point-in-time restore for block blobs, which depends on versioning, change feed and soft delete, lets containers be rolled back to an earlier state after corruption or deletion. Geo-zone-redundant storage replicates the overwritten data to the other region and so offers no recovery from malicious change. Customer-managed keys control encryption, and lifecycle management moves or deletes data by age rather than restoring it.

prompt: A tabletop exercise shows that the restore runbooks, network diagrams and configuration database a company would need to rebuild after a destructive attack are kept only on the file servers that would be encrypted. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Encrypt the file server volumes with BitLocker
Move the documents to a hidden administrative share
Increase the snapshot frequency on the file servers
Keep protected offline or immutable copies of the documents

explanation: Microsoft's recovery planning guidance includes protecting the supporting documents and systems needed for restoration, such as procedures and network diagrams, so they survive the attack. BitLocker protects data at rest from offline theft and does not stop ransomware running with valid access. A hidden share and more frequent snapshots stay on the same servers and are lost or deleted with them.

prompt: A company backs up Azure VMs to a Recovery Services vault. The disaster recovery plan requires the company to restore VMs in the paired region whenever it chooses, including during drills, without waiting for Microsoft to declare a regional disaster. Which vault design meets the requirement?

options.text: Geo-redundant storage with Cross Region Restore enabled
Geo-redundant storage with the default restore settings
Zone-redundant storage with immutability enabled
Locally redundant storage with enhanced soft delete

explanation: Cross Region Restore on a geo-redundant vault lets the customer restore from the secondary region on demand, which supports drills and customer-initiated recovery. Geo-redundant storage without that feature makes the secondary data usable only after Microsoft declares a disaster. Zone-redundant and locally redundant storage keep all copies in the primary region, so neither supports restoring in the paired region.

prompt: A board review finds that almost all of a company's security budget goes to preventive controls, and that the company has no tested way to keep critical processes running during an intrusion. The board wants the security strategy aligned with business resilience. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Add a second firewall vendor to strengthen the network perimeter
Assume compromise and balance investment across prevention, response and recovery
Transfer the residual risk to an insurer by buying a larger cyber insurance policy with ransom cover
Freeze new projects until all known vulnerabilities are remediated

explanation: Resilience means assuming that attackers will sometimes succeed and investing so that critical operations continue and recover quickly, alongside prevention. A second firewall vendor adds more prevention and leaves the gap in response and recovery. Insurance may offset financial loss but does not restore operations, and freezing projects until there are no vulnerabilities is unachievable and harms the business the strategy should support.

prompt: A company runs critical Azure VMs on Windows Server Datacenter: Azure Edition. Monthly reboots for security updates cause the business to delay patching by several weeks. The architect must evaluate an option that applies most security updates promptly without restarting the VMs. Which option should be recommended?

options.text: A maintenance configuration with a weekly reboot window
A one-time update deployment from Azure Update Manager
Hotpatch delivered through automatic VM guest patching
A failover with Azure Site Recovery before each patch cycle

explanation: Hotpatch on Windows Server Azure Edition installs security updates into running processes without a restart in most months, which removes the main reason the business delays patching. A weekly maintenance window and a one-time deployment still install updates that need a reboot. Failing over with Azure Site Recovery moves the workload but adds operational effort and does not remove the restart requirement.

prompt: An architect is hardening Azure Backup against an attacker who obtains privileged credentials and tries to destroy backups before deploying ransomware. Which two measures should the architect recommend? (Choose two.)

options.text: Require multi-user authorization for critical vault operations
Increase the backup frequency of all protected items
Place the vault in the same resource group as the workloads
Enable and lock immutability on the vault
Enable Cross Region Restore on the vault

explanation: Multi-user authorization requires approval from a separate Resource Guard owner for destructive operations, and locked immutability prevents recovery points from being removed or shortened before expiry. Increasing backup frequency creates more recovery points but does not protect them. Placing the vault with the workloads does not add protection, and Cross Region Restore addresses regional outages rather than malicious deletion.

prompt: A company is following the Zero Trust adoption framework. Business leaders want an in-product view, based on live data, of progress against metrics that are aligned to the framework's business scenarios. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: The Zero Trust initiative in Microsoft Security Exposure Management
The compliance score for a custom assessment in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
The secure score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
The identity secure score in Microsoft Entra ID

explanation: The Zero Trust initiative in Microsoft Security Exposure Management is aligned with the Zero Trust adoption framework and reports metrics by business scenario from real-time data. The Compliance Manager score measures progress against regulations, the Defender for Cloud secure score measures cloud resource posture, and the identity secure score covers only identity settings, so none of them tracks the framework's scenarios.

prompt: After a competitor is shut down for two weeks by ransomware, a company's executives ask the security architect to use the Zero Trust adoption framework. Their priority is to contain an intrusion and recover quickly if one occurs. Which business scenario from the framework should anchor the plan?

options.text: Secure remote and hybrid work
Meet regulatory and compliance requirements
Identify and protect sensitive business data
Prevent or reduce business damage from a breach

explanation: The scenario 'Prevent or reduce business damage from a breach' covers breach prevention and recovery infrastructure, which matches the stated priority of containment and fast recovery. 'Secure remote and hybrid work' focuses on identities and devices for access, 'Meet regulatory and compliance requirements' focuses on regulation, and 'Identify and protect sensitive business data' focuses on data discovery and protection.

prompt: A security team has started enabling Conditional Access and device compliance, but executives will not fund the wider Zero Trust programme because they cannot see which business risks and outcomes it addresses. According to the Zero Trust adoption framework, which lifecycle phase did the team skip?

options.text: Ready
Define strategy
Adopt
Govern

explanation: In the Define strategy phase the organisation builds a business case focused on the outcomes most closely aligned with its risks and strategic goals, which is what the executives are missing. Ready is about a multi-layer deployment strategy and adjusting guidance to the environment, Adopt is incremental implementation, and Govern tracks and measures the success of the deployment.

prompt: Data scientists at a company download models from public repositories and deploy them directly to Azure Machine Learning endpoints. The architect must align the platform with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark control that addresses backdoored or unverified models. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Add input and output content filtering to every endpoint
Require private endpoints and disable public network access for the machine learning workspace
Allow deployments only from an approved model registry by using Azure Policy
Add safety system messages to every model deployment

explanation: The benchmark's AI-1 control, Ensure use of approved models, calls for a central registry of verified models and enforcement, for example an Azure Policy assignment with the deny effect that blocks deployments from unapproved sources. Content filtering and safety system messages address prompt-based attacks at run time, not model provenance. Private endpoints reduce network exposure but do not verify the model that is deployed.

prompt: A company is releasing a public customer service chatbot built on Azure OpenAI. The design must follow the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark guidance for detecting and blocking prompt injection in user input and harmful content in responses. What should the architect include?

options.text: Azure AI Content Safety applied to both prompts and model outputs
An approved model registry enforced through Azure Policy
Customer-managed keys for the Azure OpenAI resource
Privileged Identity Management for the development team

explanation: The benchmark's AI-2 control, Implement multi-layered content filtering, recommends validating inputs and outputs, for example with Azure AI Content Safety and its prompt shields. An approved model registry addresses model provenance, customer-managed keys address encryption at rest, and Privileged Identity Management limits administrator access, none of which inspects prompts or responses.

prompt: An IT support agent built on an Azure AI service calls internal APIs through plugins. A review finds that the agent's identity holds the Contributor role on the whole subscription, although it only needs to read one knowledge base. Which recommendation aligns with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark?

options.text: Add a system message that tells the agent never to create, modify or delete resources
Send all agent activity to a Log Analytics workspace
Schedule quarterly red team exercises against the agent
Limit the agent's functions to read-only access on the required resources

explanation: The benchmark's AI-4 control, Apply least privilege for agent functions, requires agent functions and plugins to have only the minimum permissions for their purpose, so a compromised agent cannot change other resources. A system message guides behaviour but is not an enforcement boundary. Logging and red teaming help detect and find weaknesses, but neither removes the excessive permission.

prompt: A finance department plans an AI agent that can issue customer refunds in the payment system. The architect must apply the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark control that prevents the agent from completing high-impact actions on its own. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Filter the agent's responses with Azure AI Content Safety
Route refund actions through a human approval workflow before execution
Deploy the agent only from the approved model registry
Apply rate limits and quotas to the agent's refund API in Azure API Management

explanation: The benchmark's AI-5 control, Ensure human-in-the-loop, calls for human review and approval of critical actions, for example a workflow in Azure Logic Apps that pauses the process until a reviewer approves. Content filtering blocks harmful text but does not approve transactions. An approved model registry governs model provenance, and rate limiting reduces the volume of abuse without adding a human decision.

prompt: A product team wants to find jailbreak and prompt injection weaknesses in its generative AI application before each release, and to repeat the tests automatically in the CI/CD pipeline. Which approach aligns with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark?

options.text: Enable threat protection for AI services in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Assign Azure Policy initiatives to the AI resource group
Run continuous AI red teaming with tools such as PyRIT
Maintain a custom blocklist in Azure AI Content Safety

explanation: The benchmark's AI-7 control, Perform continuous AI Red Teaming, recommends adversarial testing with tools such as PyRIT or the AI Red Teaming Agent, integrated into development pipelines. Threat protection for AI services detects attacks against the running application rather than finding weaknesses before release. Azure Policy governs resource configuration, and a blocklist filters known terms without testing the application's resistance.

prompt: A company's security operations team must be alerted when users attempt jailbreaks against production Azure OpenAI deployments, and must be able to investigate those alerts with the rest of its security signals. Which capability aligns with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark guidance on AI monitoring?

options.text: Scheduled adversarial tests that use PyRIT
An approved model registry in Azure Machine Learning enforced with Azure Policy
Safety system messages on each deployment
Threat protection for AI services in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

explanation: The benchmark's AI-6 control, Establish monitoring and detection, recommends Microsoft Defender for Cloud threat protection for AI services to detect activity such as jailbreak attempts at run time. PyRIT tests find weaknesses before or between releases but do not alert on real attacks. A model registry governs which models are deployed, and safety system messages are a preventive measure that produces no alerts.

prompt: An attacker publishes a malicious version of an open-source package that a company's build pipeline pulls automatically. The architect must recommend a control that addresses this software supply chain risk before the code is released. What should be recommended?

options.text: Dependency scanning in the pipeline with packages taken from curated feeds
Dynamic application security testing against the production site after every release
A web application firewall in front of the deployed application
Code signing applied to the final compiled binaries

explanation: Software composition analysis in the pipeline, combined with approved package feeds, identifies vulnerable or malicious dependencies before they are built into a release. Dynamic testing and a web application firewall act on the running application and would not reveal a compromised dependency. Signing the final binaries proves who built them, but it would sign the malicious component along with everything else.

prompt: A company's risk register lists theft of intellectual property by departing employees as a top threat. The architect is mapping threats to capabilities by using the Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures. Which capability addresses this insider threat most directly?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management
Microsoft Entra ID Protection

explanation: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management correlates signals such as resignation dates and unusual file activity to detect risky behaviour by people inside the organisation. Defender for Identity detects attacks against on-premises Active Directory identities, and Entra ID Protection detects compromised credentials and risky sign-ins. Defender External Attack Surface Management discovers internet-facing assets and has no view of employee activity.

prompt: An external attack begins with a phishing email, moves to a compromised laptop, then to stolen credentials and lateral movement. A company's teams currently investigate separate alerts in separate consoles. Which capability in the Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures correlates these signals into one incident?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
Microsoft Defender XDR
Microsoft Intune

explanation: Microsoft Defender XDR correlates alerts from email, endpoints, identities and cloud apps into a single incident that follows the attack chain. Defender for Cloud protects cloud workloads and posture rather than email and endpoint attack chains. Purview Data Loss Prevention controls the movement of sensitive data, and Intune manages device configuration and compliance rather than correlating attacks.

prompt: A company runs workloads in Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. The architect needs one set of security controls with implementation guidance for each cloud and mappings to frameworks such as CIS, NIST and PCI DSS. Which resource should the architect adopt?

options.text: The CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark
The Azure Well-Architected Framework Security pillar
The Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures
The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark

explanation: The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark defines controls grouped by security domain, with guidance for multiple clouds and mappings to industry frameworks. The CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark covers Azure only. The Well-Architected Framework Security pillar gives design guidance for individual workloads, and the Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures describe how capabilities fit together rather than providing a control list.

prompt: A review against the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark finds that a company's Azure SQL databases and storage accounts accept connections on their public endpoints, limited only by IP firewall rules. Which design change best aligns with the benchmark's network security guidance for platform services?

options.text: Use private endpoints and disable public network access
Enable Azure DDoS Protection on the virtual networks
Enable virtual network flow logs for the workload subnets
Place Azure Front Door in front of the storage accounts

explanation: The benchmark recommends securing cloud services with network controls by giving them private access points and disabling public network access where possible. DDoS Protection defends public IP addresses against volumetric attacks and does not remove the public exposure. Flow logs provide visibility only, and Azure Front Door is a public entry point for web content that does not make the database and storage endpoints private.

prompt: A managed service provider administers a company's Microsoft 365 tenant. A supply chain risk assessment finds that the provider's staff hold standing Global Administrator access through the partner relationship. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Create a shared Global Administrator account for the provider
Replace it with granular delegated admin privileges that are least-privilege and time-bound
Invite the provider's staff as guest users and assign them permanent Global Administrator roles
Keep the existing delegation and review the provider annually

explanation: Granular delegated admin privileges let the customer grant a partner specific roles for a limited duration instead of standing Global Administrator access, which limits the damage if the provider is compromised. A shared account removes individual accountability. Permanent Global Administrator roles for guests and keeping the existing delegation both leave the provider with standing full control of the tenant.

prompt: A company treats any connection from its office network as trusted and skips multifactor authentication for those sign-ins. The architect must bring the access design in line with Zero Trust. Which change should be recommended?

options.text: Add the branch office address ranges to the trusted locations
Require a VPN connection to the office network before users can reach any cloud application
Evaluate every request on identity, device health and risk, regardless of network
Deploy a second perimeter firewall from a different vendor

explanation: The verify explicitly principle requires authenticating and authorising each request on all available data points, such as identity, device health and anomalies, rather than trusting a network location. Adding more trusted ranges and forcing traffic through a VPN both extend the implicit trust in the network. A second perimeter firewall strengthens the perimeter model that Zero Trust moves away from.

prompt: During an architecture review, the team sorts design decisions by the Zero Trust principle they implement, using Microsoft's definitions. Which two decisions implement the assume breach principle? (Choose two.)

options.text: Segmenting access to minimise the blast radius of a compromise
Authenticating each request by using all available data points
Using analytics to gain visibility and drive threat detection
Granting administrators just-in-time and just-enough access

explanation: Microsoft defines assume breach as minimising blast radius and segmenting access, verifying end-to-end encryption, and using analytics for visibility, threat detection and improved defences. Authenticating each request on all available data points is the verify explicitly principle. Just-in-time and just-enough access is how Microsoft defines the use least privileged access principle.

prompt: A team has threat-modelled its first generative AI workload with STRIDE only. The architect is aligning the organisation's AI security process with the Secure AI guidance in the Cloud Adoption Framework. What should the architect add to the risk discovery step?

options.text: A replacement of STRIDE with CVSS scoring of the model
A review against MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Generative AI risk
A mapping of the workload to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
An assessment against the CIS benchmark for Windows Server

explanation: The Secure AI guidance says to start from an established threat model and then check AI-specific coverage against knowledge bases such as MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Generative AI risk. CVSS scores known software vulnerabilities and is not a threat modelling method. ATT&CK for ICS addresses industrial control systems, and a Windows Server benchmark hardens an operating system rather than identifying AI attack techniques.

prompt: Business units at a company have created AI endpoints, models and agents in many subscriptions without telling the security team. According to the Cloud Adoption Framework Secure AI guidance, what should the architect establish first in order to protect these resources?

options.text: Customer-managed keys on the AI resources already known
A red team exercise against the main customer chatbot
A deny policy on all AI services until an audit is complete
An AI asset inventory kept current by automated discovery

explanation: The guidance starts protection with an inventory of AI assets that is maintained through automated scanning and regular validation, because unknown resources cannot be secured. Customer-managed keys and a red team exercise only cover the resources the team already knows about. Blocking all AI services stops the business from adopting AI and still does not reveal what has been deployed.

prompt: A company's public-facing AI assistant is grounded on a search index that also contains internal confidential documents. The architect must apply the Cloud Adoption Framework guidance for protecting AI data. What should be recommended?

options.text: Define data boundaries so the assistant is grounded only on data suited to its audience
Add a system message that instructs the model never to reveal content from internal documents
Filter the assistant's responses for a list of confidential keywords
Apply request rate limits to the assistant's public API

explanation: The Secure AI guidance calls for data boundaries, so that an application is given only data appropriate to the users it serves and a public assistant never has confidential content to leak. A system message and keyword filtering try to stop disclosure after the model already has the data and can be bypassed by prompt injection. Rate limiting slows extraction but does not prevent it.

prompt: A workload runs in one flat virtual network, and every component uses the same identity with a broad role on the resource group. The architect evaluates it against the Azure Well-Architected Framework Security pillar. Which recommendation should be made?

options.text: Scale the compute tier up to absorb attack traffic
Consolidate all components further onto one shared user-assigned managed identity
Build segmentation across network, identity and resource organisation
Distribute the components across availability zones

explanation: The Security pillar recommends deliberate segmentation and perimeters that cover networks, roles and responsibilities, workload identities and resource organisation, which limits lateral movement after a breach. Scaling up and using availability zones address performance and reliability rather than containment. One shared identity widens the blast radius further.

prompt: An architect must evaluate the security design of one production workload in Azure and produce prioritised recommendations for its owners. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: A cloud adoption strategy assessment for the whole organisation
A Well-Architected Review of the workload against the Security pillar
An Azure landing zone review of the platform subscriptions
A review of Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal

explanation: The Azure Well-Architected Framework and its review are scoped to an individual workload and produce recommendations by pillar, including Security. A cloud adoption strategy assessment and a landing zone review look at the organisation and the shared platform rather than one workload's design. Microsoft Secure Score reports on Microsoft 365 and identity posture settings, not on the architecture of an Azure workload.

prompt: A company moving to Azure has no defined responsibilities for security architecture, posture management, security operations or governance, risk and compliance, and no process for integrating security into each phase of adoption. Which guidance should the architect use to design this?

options.text: The Azure Well-Architected Framework Security pillar
The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark control list
An Azure Architecture Center reference architecture
The Cloud Adoption Framework Secure methodology

explanation: The Cloud Adoption Framework Secure methodology addresses organisation-wide concerns such as security teams and roles, posture modernisation, incident preparedness and sustaining security across the adoption journey. The Well-Architected Framework Security pillar is workload-level design guidance. The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark lists technical controls, and a reference architecture describes one solution, so none of these defines the operating model.

prompt: Forty application teams will receive their own subscriptions in an Azure landing zone. Security requires that every new subscription automatically sends diagnostic logs to the central workspace and cannot create public IP addresses for internal workloads. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Policy assignments at management group scope that subscriptions inherit
A central team that deploys every resource on behalf of the application teams
A manual security checklist completed for each new subscription
Resource locks applied to each resource group after deployment

explanation: Policy-driven governance is an Azure landing zone design principle: guardrails are assigned to management groups and inherited by every subscription placed beneath them. A central team deploying everything conflicts with subscription democratisation and does not scale. A manual checklist is not enforced, and resource locks prevent deletion or modification but cannot require logging or block public IP addresses.

prompt: A company uses the Azure landing zone management group hierarchy. A new internal payroll application needs connectivity to on-premises systems through the hub network and must not expose public endpoints. Under which management group should its subscription be placed?

options.text: Online
Sandbox
Corp
Connectivity

explanation: The Corp management group is for internal-facing workloads that need private connectivity, and its policies restrict public exposure. Online is for internet-facing workloads. Sandbox is for isolated experimentation with no connection to corporate networks, and Connectivity is a platform management group for shared network resources such as hubs, not for application workloads.

prompt: Developers want to experiment with newly released Azure services. The architect must let them do so without creating risk to production workloads or to the corporate network, while keeping the experiments inside the governed Azure landing zone structure. What should be recommended?

options.text: A dedicated resource group in an existing Corp production subscription, with tags for cost tracking
A new spoke network in the Connectivity subscription
A subscription in the Decommissioned management group
Subscriptions in the Sandbox management group, isolated from Corp and Online

explanation: The Sandbox management group holds subscriptions for testing and exploration that are isolated from corporate and online landing zones and carry a less restrictive policy set. A resource group in a Corp production subscription puts experiments beside production under production policies. The Connectivity subscription is for shared platform networking, and Decommissioned holds cancelled subscriptions awaiting deletion.

prompt: An application team asks for the Owner role at the Landing Zones management group so it can manage its three subscriptions more conveniently. Which recommendation aligns with Azure landing zone guidance?

options.text: Grant Owner at the management group and require PIM activation
Grant the team access at the scope of its own subscriptions
Grant Contributor at the tenant root management group
Grant User Access Administrator at the management group

explanation: Landing zone guidance advises against assigning workload teams roles at management group scopes; teams are given control of their own subscriptions, in line with subscription democratisation. Owner at the management group, even through PIM, would give the team rights over every other team's subscriptions. Contributor at the tenant root and User Access Administrator at the management group are broader still.

prompt: A company runs 30 unrelated applications in one large Azure subscription. Policy exceptions for one application weaken controls for the others, and a single compromised deployment identity can reach every workload. Which design change aligns with Azure landing zone principles?

options.text: Give each workload its own subscription under the appropriate management group
Give each workload its own resource group and a consistent set of tags
Give each workload its own virtual network and network security groups inside the shared subscription
Give each workload its own Microsoft Entra tenant and subscription

explanation: Azure landing zones treat the subscription as the unit of management, policy and scale, so each workload gets its own subscription that inherits guardrails from its management group. Resource groups, tags and separate virtual networks inside one subscription still share the same policy assignments and subscription-level roles. A tenant for each workload fragments identity and creates heavy management overhead.

prompt: A company's developers have several times committed API keys to Git repositories. The architect is adding DevSecOps controls that follow Cloud Adoption Framework guidance. Which control addresses this at the earliest effective point?

options.text: Dynamic application security testing of every build in the staging environment
A live-site penetration test once each quarter
Credential scanning that blocks secrets when code is committed or pushed
A threat modelling session at the start of each feature

explanation: Credential scanning at the commit stage, with protection that blocks the push, stops secrets from entering the repository history. Dynamic testing and penetration testing run against deployed applications and would find the problem late, if at all. Threat modelling identifies design risks but does not detect a key pasted into source code.

prompt: Penetration tests on a company's applications repeatedly find design flaws, such as missing trust boundaries, that are expensive to fix after release. Which DevSecOps practice should the architect add to the plan and develop stage?

options.text: Container image vulnerability scanning
Security smoke tests after deployment
Credential scanning in repositories
Threat modelling of each new design

explanation: Threat modelling during planning and design identifies missing trust boundaries and other architectural weaknesses before code is written, when they are cheapest to fix. Image scanning and credential scanning find vulnerable components and exposed secrets rather than design flaws. Security smoke tests confirm a deployment's basic security state and run far too late to influence the design.

prompt: Infrastructure-as-code templates at a company have deployed storage accounts with public access enabled several times. The architect must add a DevSecOps control that catches the misconfiguration before any resource is created. What should be recommended?

options.text: A quarterly audit of the resources that have been deployed
Scanning of the templates in the pipeline before deployment
Dynamic security testing of the application's web front end
Peer review limited to the application source code

explanation: Scanning infrastructure-as-code in the build and test stage finds insecure settings in the templates so the pipeline can fail before deployment. A quarterly audit detects the problem only after the resource has been exposed. Dynamic testing of the web front end and peer review of application code do not examine the infrastructure templates.

prompt: A deployment pipeline authenticates to Azure with a service principal that holds the Owner role on a subscription and uses a client secret that expires in two years. The architect must reduce the risk of the pipeline being used to compromise the environment. What should be recommended?

options.text: Workload identity federation with a role scoped to what the pipeline deploys
Annual rotation of the existing client secret
Storage of the client secret in a secret pipeline variable that only administrators can edit
A personal access token from an administrator account

explanation: Workload identity federation removes the stored secret by exchanging short-lived tokens, and scoping the role to the resources the pipeline deploys applies least privilege. Rotating the secret each year or hiding it in a pipeline variable still leaves a long-lived credential with Owner rights that can be stolen. An administrator's personal access token ties the pipeline to a human's broad privileges.

prompt: As part of governance under the Cloud Adoption Framework, a company wants to measure its Azure subscriptions continuously against a baseline of security controls and track the result as a score. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Advisor recommendations for cost, performance and operational excellence, reviewed monthly
Azure Monitor workbooks built on activity log data
Microsoft Defender for Cloud with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark
Microsoft Entra identity secure score

explanation: Defender for Cloud assesses resources against the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark by default and expresses the result as a secure score, which the landing zone security guidance uses as the baseline. Azure Advisor cost and performance recommendations and activity log workbooks are not a security control baseline. The identity secure score covers Microsoft Entra settings only, not Azure resources.

prompt: A company with a small security team is deciding between adopting a Microsoft software as a service copilot and self-hosting an open-source model on virtual machines. Which statement about the AI shared responsibility model should inform its secure AI adoption strategy?

options.text: Microsoft is responsible for classifying the company's data in both options
The software as a service option makes the company secure the model hosting infrastructure
Responsibilities are divided identically in the two options
Self-hosting moves responsibility for model safety and AI infrastructure to the company

explanation: In the AI shared responsibility model, the customer takes on more as it moves from software as a service toward infrastructure as a service; when it self-hosts a model it must secure the infrastructure and provide the model's safety systems. Data classification and governance remain the customer's responsibility in every model. With a software as a service copilot Microsoft operates the hosting infrastructure, so the division is not identical.

prompt: A company uses the Microsoft Defender products for endpoints, email and identities. It also needs detections on firewall logs, AWS CloudTrail and custom application logs, and wants analysts to work one correlated incident queue. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Defender XDR alone, with custom detection rules written for every log source
Azure Monitor alerts on a Log Analytics workspace
Microsoft Sentinel connected to the Defender portal with Defender XDR
Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts exported to email

explanation: Microsoft Sentinel provides SIEM ingestion and analytics for third-party and custom sources, and connecting it to the Defender portal unifies its incidents with Defender XDR in one queue. Defender XDR alone correlates the Microsoft Defender workloads but is not designed to ingest arbitrary firewall and application logs. Azure Monitor alerts and exported Defender for Cloud alerts provide no cross-domain incident correlation.

prompt: A company must keep high-volume firewall and proxy logs for seven years for possible investigations. The logs are rarely queried and are not used by real-time detections. The architect must minimise cost while keeping the data queryable from Microsoft Sentinel. Where should the logs be stored?

options.text: The Microsoft Sentinel data lake tier
The analytics tier with maximum retention
Advanced hunting tables in Defender XDR
Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium)

explanation: The data lake tier is intended for low-cost, long-term storage of high-volume data and supports total retention of up to 12 years. The analytics tier supports real-time detections but its retention can be set to at most two years and it costs more. Defender XDR keeps hunting data for 30 days by default, and Purview Audit stores Microsoft 365 audit records rather than firewall logs.

prompt: A company's legal department requires that Microsoft 365 audit records for members of the executive team are kept for 10 years. Records for other users can follow the default retention. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Audit (Standard) with weekly exports of search results
A litigation hold on each executive mailbox
The Microsoft Sentinel analytics tier with the executives' tables set to maximum retention
Audit (Premium) with the 10-year add-on and a custom retention policy

explanation: Audit (Premium) supports custom audit log retention policies, and the 10-year audit log retention add-on licence allows a policy that keeps the executives' records for 10 years. Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days. A litigation hold preserves mailbox content rather than audit records, and the Sentinel analytics tier retains data for at most two years.

prompt: A multinational has one security operations team. Regulation requires that security logs from European subsidiaries are stored in Europe, while other logs are stored in the United States. Analysts must be able to investigate across all the data. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: One Microsoft Sentinel workspace in a United States region
Sentinel workspaces in each geography with cross-workspace queries
A separate Microsoft Entra tenant and security team per region
Regional storage accounts that hold logs without a SIEM

explanation: A workspace stores data in its own region, so regional workspaces satisfy residency while cross-workspace queries and central management let one team investigate everywhere. A single United States workspace breaks the European residency requirement. Separate tenants and teams remove the single operations team, and storage accounts without a SIEM provide retention but no detection or investigation.

prompt: A managed security service provider will operate Microsoft Sentinel for 25 customers. Each customer's data must stay in the customer's own tenant, and the provider's analysts must use their own identities to work across all the customer workspaces. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Guest accounts for every analyst in every customer tenant
A shared workspace in the provider tenant for all customer logs
Azure Lighthouse delegation of the customer workspaces
Granular delegated admin privileges for each customer

explanation: Azure Lighthouse delegates Azure resources such as Sentinel workspaces to the provider's tenant, so analysts use their own identities at scale while the data remains with each customer. Guest accounts in every tenant require separate accounts and switching between tenants. A shared provider workspace moves the data out of the customer tenants, and granular delegated admin privileges govern partner administration of Microsoft 365 services rather than Azure resource access.

prompt: A company must collect Windows security events and Linux syslog from on-premises servers and AWS EC2 instances into Microsoft Sentinel, with the collection rules managed centrally from Azure. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: The legacy Log Analytics agent installed on each server by a configuration management tool
The Azure Site Recovery mobility service on each server
Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors on each server
Azure Arc-enabled servers with Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules

explanation: Azure Arc projects non-Azure machines into Azure so that Azure Monitor Agent can be deployed and governed with data collection rules that send events to the Sentinel workspace. The Log Analytics agent has been retired in favour of Azure Monitor Agent. The Site Recovery mobility service replicates disks, and Defender for Identity sensors monitor identity infrastructure such as domain controllers rather than collecting general server logs.

prompt: A company's analysts need to detect suspicious AWS management activity, such as unusual IAM changes, and correlate it with Microsoft Entra sign-in data in Microsoft Sentinel. What should the architect include in the design?

options.text: The Sentinel Amazon Web Services connector that ingests CloudTrail logs
Azure Monitor Agent installed on every EC2 instance
Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes for the company's EKS clusters
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint onboarding of every EC2 instance through Defender for Cloud

explanation: AWS management-plane activity is recorded in CloudTrail, and the Sentinel Amazon Web Services connector ingests those logs so analytics rules can correlate them with other sources. Azure Monitor Agent and Defender for Endpoint collect telemetry from inside the operating system of an instance and do not see IAM changes made through the AWS control plane. Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes manages clusters and does not ingest CloudTrail.

prompt: A company wants hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks to be contained while they are in progress, by automatically isolating the compromised devices and user accounts, without the security team building and maintaining response workflows. Which capability should the architect recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks run by automation rules
Automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR
Scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel
Device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune

explanation: Automatic attack disruption uses correlated Defender XDR signals to contain compromised devices and users during an attack, and it is built in rather than authored by the customer. Sentinel playbooks can take similar actions but must be designed, built and maintained by the team. Scheduled analytics rules only detect, and Intune compliance policies assess device configuration rather than respond to an active attack.

prompt: When Microsoft Sentinel creates an incident from a specific set of analytics rules, a company wants a ticket opened in its IT service management tool and the incident enriched with data from a threat intelligence service. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: A scheduled analytics rule with extra entity mappings
A custom detection rule in Microsoft Defender XDR
An automation rule that runs a playbook built on Azure Logic Apps
A transformation in a data collection rule

explanation: Automation rules trigger on incident creation and can call playbooks, which are Azure Logic Apps workflows with connectors to external systems such as ticketing and enrichment services. Analytics rules and Defender XDR custom detection rules generate alerts and incidents but do not orchestrate external actions. A data collection rule transformation changes data at ingestion time and has no knowledge of incidents.

prompt: A security operations team wants new Microsoft Sentinel incidents to be assigned to an owner, tagged and, for a known benign pattern, closed automatically. No external systems are involved, and the team wants the least cost and maintenance. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Playbooks on the Azure Logic Apps Standard plan
Azure Functions triggered through Azure Event Grid
Suppression settings on the analytics rules
Automation rules without playbooks

explanation: Automation rules can assign owners, add tags, change status and close incidents directly, with no workflow to build or pay for. Logic Apps playbooks and Azure Functions could do the same but add cost and maintenance that the requirement does not justify. Rule suppression stops an analytics rule from running for a period after it fires and does not assign, tag or close incidents.

prompt: During a proactive hunt, analysts write a KQL query that reliably identifies a credential theft technique. The architect is evaluating the hunting workflow and wants findings like this to produce alerts in future without manual effort. What should the workflow include?

options.text: Converting proven hunting queries into detection rules
Saving the query results as hunting bookmarks
Publishing the query results in a workbook
Loading the query results into a watchlist

explanation: A mature hunting workflow turns successful hypotheses into scheduled analytics or custom detection rules, so the technique is detected continuously. Bookmarks preserve interesting results for an investigation but do not run again. Workbooks visualise data, and watchlists hold reference data for use in queries, so neither generates alerts on its own.

prompt: An evaluation of a company's incident response process shows that the same attack technique succeeded in three separate incidents, because detections and automated responses were never updated after each one was closed. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Extend log retention in the analytics tier to two years so evidence is kept for later incidents
Add a post-incident review that feeds changes into detections and automation
Hire additional first-line analysts for incident triage
Raise the default severity of all incidents to high

explanation: An incident response lifecycle ends with post-incident learning, where findings are turned into new or tuned detections, automation and preventive controls. Longer retention keeps evidence but changes nothing about detection. More triage analysts and a higher default severity affect how quickly incidents are handled, not whether the lessons from them are applied.

prompt: An architect wants to see which adversary tactics and techniques are covered by a company's active Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules, and how coverage would change if rule templates that are available but not yet enabled were turned on. What should the architect use?

options.text: The threat intelligence page with imported indicators
The Content hub list of installed solutions
The MITRE ATT&CK page with simulated rules selected
A workbook that reports data connector health

explanation: The MITRE ATT&CK page in Microsoft Sentinel maps active rules to tactics and techniques, and its simulated option shows the coverage the organisation could have with additional rules. The threat intelligence page manages indicators rather than rule coverage. The Content hub lists what is installed without mapping it to techniques, and a connector health workbook reports ingestion status only.

prompt: A manufacturer monitors programmable logic controllers and SCADA systems with Microsoft Defender for IoT and sends the alerts to Microsoft Sentinel. The architect must evaluate detection coverage for attacks on this plant equipment. Which knowledge base should be used?

options.text: The MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise matrix
The MITRE ATT&CK Mobile matrix
The MITRE ATLAS matrix
The MITRE ATT&CK for ICS matrix

explanation: ATT&CK for ICS describes adversary behaviour against industrial control systems, and Defender for IoT maps its alerts to ICS techniques. The Enterprise matrix covers operating systems, cloud, network and container platforms, and the Mobile matrix covers Android and iOS devices. MITRE ATLAS catalogues attacks on AI systems.

prompt: A company's estate consists of Windows and Linux servers, containers, Azure infrastructure, Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra ID. A colleague suggests that MITRE ATT&CK cannot be used to assess detection coverage for the cloud services. Which matrix should the architect use for this estate?

options.text: The Enterprise matrix, which includes cloud, identity provider and container platforms
The Mobile matrix, which includes cloud-connected Android and iOS devices and their network effects
The ICS matrix, which includes control servers and field controllers
The ATLAS matrix, which includes machine learning models and pipelines

explanation: The ATT&CK Enterprise matrix covers Windows, Linux and macOS along with network devices, containers and cloud platforms including IaaS, SaaS, office suites and identity providers, so the colleague's claim is incorrect. The Mobile matrix addresses techniques against Android and iOS devices, the ICS matrix addresses industrial control systems, and MITRE ATLAS catalogues attacks on AI systems rather than on this estate.

prompt: A MITRE ATT&CK coverage review shows that a company has many detections for initial access and execution, and none for lateral movement or exfiltration. The detection engineering team has limited capacity. How should the architect prioritise new detections?

options.text: Enable every available rule template to fill the matrix
Target uncovered techniques used by threat actors relevant to the company
Retire the existing rules for tactics that are already covered
Keep the focus on initial access, because strong prevention makes later detections unnecessary

explanation: Coverage work is most valuable when it targets gaps in techniques that relevant threat actors actually use, supported by the data sources the company has. Enabling every template creates noise and cost without regard to relevance. Retiring working rules reduces coverage, and focusing only on initial access ignores the assumption that some attackers will get past it.

prompt: A company is licensed for Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) and is listing new requirements for its audit design. Which two requirements need Audit (Premium)? (Choose two.)

options.text: Custom audit log retention policies
Searching the audit log for user activity
Exporting audit search results to a file
Intelligent insights for forensic investigations

explanation: Audit (Premium) adds custom audit log retention policies, longer default retention for key workloads and intelligent insights that help forensic investigations. Searching the audit log and exporting the results are available in Audit (Standard), which retains records for 180 days.

prompt: A company runs autonomous AI agents that authenticate with Microsoft Entra Agent ID identities. The architect must ensure that an agent which Microsoft Entra ID Protection flags as high risk cannot obtain tokens. Which design should be recommended?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy for all users that requires multifactor authentication
A user risk policy that requires a secure password change
A sign-in frequency session control applied to all cloud apps
A Conditional Access policy for agent identities that blocks on agent risk

explanation: Conditional Access for agents can target agent identities, use agent risk as a condition and apply the block control. A policy scoped to all users does not apply to agent identities, and an agent cannot complete multifactor authentication. A user risk policy with password change and a sign-in frequency control are designed for human users and do not act on agent risk.

prompt: A company wants only AI agents created from two approved agent identity blueprints to authenticate in its tenant. Agents that are created from those blueprints in future must be allowed without any change to the policy. Which Conditional Access design should the architect recommend?

options.text: Block all agent identities and exclude the two approved blueprints
Block all agent identities and exclude each approved agent individually
Require a compliant device for all agent identities in the tenant
Allow agent identities only from a named location of trusted addresses

explanation: Targeting or excluding an agent identity blueprint covers every agent identity derived from it, including agents created later, so excluding the approved blueprints from a block policy meets the requirement. Excluding individual agents means the policy must be edited for each new agent. For agent identities the only grant control is block and the only condition is agent risk, so a compliant device requirement or a location condition cannot be used.

prompt: A governance standard states that every AI agent identity must have a person who is accountable for its purpose and lifecycle. That person must be able to disable the agent but must not be able to change its configuration or credentials. Which relationship in Microsoft Entra Agent ID should the architect require?

options.text: An owner assigned to each agent identity
A sponsor assigned to each agent identity
A manager assigned to each agent identity
A Global Administrator named in each agent's notes

explanation: A sponsor is accountable for an agent's purpose and lifecycle and can disable or delete it, but cannot change its application settings. An owner is a technical administrator who manages configuration and credentials, which exceeds what the standard allows. A manager places the agent in the organisational hierarchy, and naming a Global Administrator in a notes field creates no enforced relationship and relies on a highly privileged role.

prompt: Remote employees need access to on-premises web applications that use Kerberos authentication. The design must provide single sign-on, apply Conditional Access before a connection reaches the application, and avoid opening inbound firewall ports. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: A point-to-site VPN that uses certificate authentication
AD FS published through Web Application Proxy servers in the perimeter network
Microsoft Entra application proxy with Kerberos constrained delegation
Azure Front Door with a web application firewall policy

explanation: Microsoft Entra application proxy uses connectors that make outbound connections only, pre-authenticates users with Microsoft Entra ID so Conditional Access applies, and uses Kerberos constrained delegation for single sign-on. A point-to-site VPN gives network-level access rather than per-application access with pre-authentication. AD FS with Web Application Proxy needs inbound publishing in the perimeter network, and Azure Front Door requires the origin to be reachable and provides no Kerberos sign-on.

prompt: Administrators connect to Azure virtual machines over RDP and SSH. The design must remove public IP addresses from the VMs and require administrators to authenticate with Microsoft Entra credentials that are subject to Conditional Access. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Public IP addresses limited to office ranges by network security groups
A site-to-site VPN with local administrator accounts on each VM
A jump server with a public IP address and a shared account
Azure Bastion combined with Microsoft Entra sign-in to the VMs

explanation: Azure Bastion provides RDP and SSH connectivity to VMs that have no public IP addresses, and Microsoft Entra sign-in to the VMs replaces local accounts with identities governed by Conditional Access and Azure roles. Restricting public IP addresses by source range still exposes management ports to the internet. A VPN with local accounts and a shared jump server account both fail the requirement for Microsoft Entra authentication.

prompt: Employees at a company sign in to several AWS accounts with separate IAM users. The architect must design access so that corporate identities, multifactor authentication and Conditional Access apply to AWS, and so that access is removed when a person leaves. What should be recommended?

options.text: Federate AWS IAM Identity Center with Microsoft Entra ID, with automatic provisioning
Keep the IAM users and require AWS virtual MFA devices and a 90-day password rotation for each of them
Deploy Microsoft Entra Domain Services and join the AWS accounts to it
Build an AD FS farm that is dedicated to AWS sign-in

explanation: Using Microsoft Entra ID as the identity provider for AWS IAM Identity Center gives single sign-on governed by Conditional Access, and provisioning removes access when the user is disabled or deleted. Separate IAM users with AWS MFA remain outside the corporate identity lifecycle. Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services for legacy workloads in Azure, and a dedicated AD FS farm adds on-premises infrastructure without Conditional Access.

prompt: A company synchronises on-premises Active Directory users to Microsoft Entra ID. It needs users to keep signing in to cloud services if the datacenter is unavailable, and it wants Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials. Which authentication method should the architect recommend?

options.text: Pass-through authentication
Password hash synchronization
Federation with AD FS
Microsoft Entra Domain Services

explanation: With password hash synchronization, Microsoft Entra ID validates sign-ins itself, so cloud authentication continues during an on-premises outage, and the synchronised hashes enable leaked credential detection. Pass-through authentication and AD FS federation both depend on on-premises servers being available to validate each sign-in. Microsoft Entra Domain Services is a managed domain service and not a sign-in method for hybrid users.

prompt: A regulator requires that the keys protecting a bank's Azure data are held in a single-tenant hardware security module, and that the bank alone controls the security domain of that module. The keys must be usable as customer-managed keys by Azure services. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Key Vault Premium
Azure Key Vault Standard
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
Platform-managed keys

explanation: Managed HSM is a single-tenant, fully managed HSM service in which the customer holds the security domain, and Azure services can use its keys as customer-managed keys. Key Vault Premium protects keys in HSMs but is a multitenant service. Key Vault Standard protects keys in software, and platform-managed keys are controlled by Microsoft rather than by the bank.

prompt: A company's Conditional Access policies require multifactor authentication and a compliant device for all users. Guests from a trusted partner already satisfy both requirements in the partner's own Microsoft Entra tenant and complain about a second MFA prompt. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Exclude all guest and external users from the two Conditional Access policies that cause the prompt
Enable B2B direct connect with the partner organisation
Create local member accounts for the partner's employees
Trust the partner's MFA and device claims in inbound cross-tenant access settings

explanation: Inbound trust settings in cross-tenant access let Conditional Access accept MFA and compliant device claims from a specific external organisation, which keeps the controls and removes the duplicate prompt. Excluding guests removes the protection for every external user. B2B direct connect enables shared channel collaboration and does not by itself trust claims, and local member accounts create extra credentials outside the partner's identity lifecycle.

prompt: Contractors who request access to a project must prove that they hold a current safety certification issued by an external training body. The company does not want to collect or store copies of the certificates. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: An access package that requires a Microsoft Entra Verified ID credential from the issuer
A B2B invitation that is redeemed with an email one-time passcode
A custom security attribute that a project manager sets on each account after seeing the certificate
A quarterly access review of the contractors' group membership

explanation: Entitlement management can require requestors to present a verifiable credential from a trusted issuer by using Microsoft Entra Verified ID, so the claim is checked cryptographically and no document copy is stored. An email one-time passcode proves control of a mailbox only. A custom security attribute records what someone typed, and an access review checks continued need without validating the certification.

prompt: A company wants administrators to satisfy phishing-resistant MFA from a privileged access workstation at the moment they delete a Conditional Access policy or change cross-tenant access settings, even when they signed in and activated their role earlier in the day. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: A PIM role setting that requires MFA on activation
Protected actions tied to an authentication context policy
A one-hour sign-in frequency for all administrators
Administrative units that contain the administrators

explanation: Protected actions assign a Conditional Access authentication context to specific high-impact permissions, so the policy is enforced when the action is attempted rather than at sign-in or role activation. PIM activation requirements are checked when the role is activated, not when the action is taken. Sign-in frequency forces periodic reauthentication without regard to the action, and administrative units scope role assignments rather than adding step-up requirements.

prompt: When a company disables a user account, the user can continue to work in Exchange Online and SharePoint until the current access token expires. The architect must close this gap so that access is withdrawn in near real time. Which capability should be included in the design?

options.text: Token protection that binds sign-in tokens to the device
Disabling persistent browser sessions for all users
Continuous access evaluation for supported services
Shorter password expiry for all user accounts

explanation: Continuous access evaluation lets supported services such as Exchange Online and SharePoint react to critical events, including an account being disabled or a password reset, and reject the token in near real time. Token protection reduces token theft by binding tokens to a device but does not revoke a valid session. Non-persistent browser sessions and shorter password expiry do not affect a token that has already been issued.

prompt: Credentials for several of a company's users appear in a public breach list. The authentication strategy must automatically require those users to remediate before they can continue to access resources, while users who are not affected see no change. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Smart lockout with a lower lockout threshold
A custom banned password list in password protection that contains the leaked passwords
Security defaults enabled for the tenant
A Conditional Access policy on user risk that requires risk remediation

explanation: Microsoft Entra ID Protection raises user risk when it detects leaked credentials, and a risk-based Conditional Access policy can require affected users to remediate, for example with a secure password change, while leaving other users alone. Smart lockout slows password guessing and does not react to leaked credentials. A banned password list restricts new password choices, and security defaults apply the same baseline to everyone without risk-based remediation.

prompt: An architect has designed a set of Conditional Access policies that implement Zero Trust for all users and applications. Before enforcement, the architect must validate the effect of the policies on real sign-ins without blocking anyone. What should be recommended?

options.text: Deploy the policies in report-only mode and review the sign-in results
Enable the policies and monitor the volume of help desk calls
Enable security defaults alongside the new policies during testing
Enforce per-user MFA while the new policies are reviewed

explanation: Report-only mode evaluates policies against real sign-ins and records what the result would have been, so gaps and unintended impact can be found before enforcement. Enabling the policies and watching help desk calls tests in production at the users' expense. Security defaults cannot be combined with Conditional Access policies, and per-user MFA is a separate legacy mechanism that reveals nothing about the new policies.

prompt: An assessment of a company's Active Directory Domain Services finds that members of Domain Admins routinely sign in to member servers and user workstations. Which hardening requirement should the architect specify to reduce credential theft?

options.text: Require passwords of at least 20 characters for Domain Admins
Limit Domain Admins to sign in only to domain controllers and privileged access workstations
Rename the built-in Administrator account in every domain
Add Domain Admins to the local Administrators group on every member server to reduce delegation errors

explanation: Credentials are exposed on any system where a privileged account signs in, so the highest-privilege accounts must be restricted to domain controllers and dedicated administrative workstations. Longer passwords do not prevent theft of hashes or tickets from the memory of a compromised host. Renaming the Administrator account is obscurity only, and adding Domain Admins to more local groups encourages wider use of those accounts.

prompt: A security assessment shows that a company's domain controllers accept unsigned LDAP binds and NTLMv1 authentication, which exposes the domain to relay and interception attacks. Which requirement should the architect specify to harden Active Directory Domain Services?

options.text: Reduce the maximum password age to 30 days
