Deploy additional read-only domain controllers
Enforce LDAP signing and channel binding and disable NTLMv1
Enable the Active Directory Recycle Bin

explanation: Requiring LDAP signing and channel binding and removing NTLMv1 closes the weak protocol paths that relay and interception attacks depend on. A shorter password age does not change the protocols in use. Read-only domain controllers reduce exposure at branch sites, and the Recycle Bin helps recover deleted objects, so neither addresses the finding.

prompt: Applications on Azure App Service keep database passwords and API keys in application settings and in deployment scripts. The architect must design secret management that removes stored credentials from code and gives each application access to its own secrets only. What should be recommended?

options.text: One shared key vault for the whole platform that all applications reach with a client secret
Azure App Configuration key-values that hold the secrets
Secrets encrypted with a team key and stored in the source repository
A key vault per application, accessed with managed identities and Azure RBAC

explanation: A separate key vault per application limits each application to its own secrets, managed identities remove the need to store any credential for reaching the vault, and Azure RBAC is the recommended authorisation model for the vault's data plane. A shared vault reached with a client secret exposes every application's secrets and leaves a credential to protect. App Configuration key-values are meant for configuration rather than secrets, and encrypted secrets in a repository still require distributing and protecting a key.

prompt: An architect is classifying assets by using the enterprise access model. The Microsoft Entra Connect server and the accounts that administer it can change identities and credentials for the whole organisation. In which part of the model do they belong?

options.text: Control plane
Management plane
Data/workload plane
User access

explanation: The control plane contains the identity systems, and the paths to them, that can grant control over everything else, so the synchronisation server and its administrators need the highest level of protection. The management plane covers enterprise-wide IT management functions, and the data/workload plane covers administration of individual workloads. User access is the pathway for ordinary users and applications.

prompt: A company's domain controllers are administered through a jump server. That jump server is patched and managed by the general server team with the same tools as line-of-business servers. How should the architect treat the jump server under the enterprise access model?

options.text: Keep it in the management plane and require MFA to sign in to it
Treat it as a workload plane asset, because it holds no business data
Treat it as a control plane asset, administered only from equally trusted systems
Allow access to it from user workstations that use Network Level Authentication

explanation: An intermediary used to administer control plane assets can be used to take control of them, so it must be protected and administered at the same level as the control plane. Leaving it in the management or workload plane lets anyone who compromises the general server tooling escalate to the domain controllers, even with MFA at sign-in. Access from user workstations exposes it to lower-trust devices.

prompt: The help desk for a company's European division must be able to reset passwords for users in that division only. It must not be able to manage users in other divisions. Which delegation design should the architect recommend?

options.text: A tenant-wide User Administrator assignment made eligible in PIM
A role assignment scoped to an administrative unit for the division
A custom role assigned at the scope of the whole tenant
A Global Reader assignment for the help desk group

explanation: Administrative units restrict a role assignment to a defined set of users, so a help desk role scoped to the division's unit can manage only those accounts. A tenant-wide User Administrator assignment, even when activated through PIM, covers all divisions. A custom role at tenant scope is also unrestricted, and Global Reader cannot reset passwords.

prompt: A review of a company's Microsoft Entra ID tenant finds 14 users with permanently active Global Administrator assignments, in addition to two emergency access accounts. Which recommendation should the architect make?

options.text: Keep the assignments permanent and rotate the passwords monthly
Move the users into a role-assignable group and give the group a permanent active role assignment
Remove every permanent assignment, including the emergency access accounts
Make the users eligible in PIM with approval, and keep only the emergency accounts active

explanation: Privileged Identity Management replaces standing access with eligible assignments that are activated just in time, with controls such as approval and MFA, while emergency access accounts stay permanently active for recovery. Password rotation leaves standing privilege in place. A role-assignable group with permanent membership only moves the standing access, and removing the emergency accounts risks locking the tenant out.

prompt: Platform engineers at a company need three Microsoft Entra roles and two Azure roles for their on-call duty. The architect wants a single just-in-time activation, with approval, to grant the whole set. What should be recommended?

options.text: PIM for Groups, with the roles assigned to a role-assignable group
Five separate eligible role assignments for each engineer
An access package that grants the five roles with no expiry
A dynamic membership group based on the job title attribute

explanation: With PIM for Groups, engineers are eligible members of a role-assignable group that holds the roles, so one activation with approval grants the complete set for a limited time. Separate eligible assignments require five activations. An access package without expiry provides standing access rather than just-in-time access, and a dynamic group grants membership automatically with no activation or approval.

prompt: Project teams at a company include employees and partner users. Each member needs a set of groups, applications and SharePoint sites. Access must be requested, approved by the project sponsor and removed automatically when it expires. Which Microsoft Entra capability should the architect recommend?

options.text: Privileged Identity Management role settings
Dynamic membership groups
Entitlement management access packages
Administrative units

explanation: Entitlement management bundles groups, applications and sites into access packages with request, approval and expiry policies for internal and external users. Privileged Identity Management governs just-in-time activation of privileged roles rather than bundles of everyday resources. Dynamic groups assign membership by attribute without request or approval, and administrative units scope administration rather than grant access.

prompt: An auditor requires that a user who holds the purchasing access package can never also obtain the payment approval access package. The control must prevent the combination rather than detect it afterwards. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy that blocks the payment application
Separation of duties settings that mark the access packages as incompatible
A quarterly access review of both access packages
Separate administrative units for the two groups of users

explanation: Entitlement management separation of duties checks stop a user from requesting an access package when they already hold one that is marked incompatible. A Conditional Access policy that blocks the application would affect legitimate approvers as well. A quarterly access review detects the conflict only after it exists, and administrative units scope administrative roles rather than control which access packages a user can hold.

prompt: An evaluation finds hundreds of guest accounts in a company's Microsoft 365 groups that nobody has confirmed are still needed. The architect must recommend a governance design that removes stale guests with minimal manual effort. What should be recommended?

options.text: A one-time review by a Global Administrator, exported to a spreadsheet for the group owners
Tighter guest invitation settings for members of the organisation
A sign-in frequency Conditional Access policy for guest users
Recurring guest access reviews that auto-apply results and remove non-responders

explanation: Recurring access reviews scoped to guests, with results applied automatically and access removed when reviewers do not respond, clean up stale guests continuously. A one-time review addresses today's guests only and still requires manual removal. Invitation restrictions limit new guests, and sign-in frequency changes how often guests authenticate, so neither removes existing unneeded access.

prompt: An architect evaluates a company's access review programme. Reviews finish on time, but one central administrator approves almost every entry without the knowledge to judge whether access is needed. Which change would most improve the programme?

options.text: Assign reviews to managers or resource owners, with recommendations and required justification
Increase the frequency of every access review to weekly
Keep the central administrator as the reviewer and extend each review period from 14 to 60 calendar days
Set the review to approve access when the reviewer does not respond

explanation: Reviews are meaningful when the reviewer knows the user's need, and decision helpers such as inactivity-based recommendations plus required justification discourage blanket approval. Weekly reviews add fatigue and make rubber-stamping more likely. A longer review period does not give the central administrator the missing knowledge, and approving on non-response removes the control altogether.

prompt: Control plane administrators at a company sometimes work from home and must administer on-premises servers remotely. The design must preserve the principle that a system is only administered from a device of equal or higher trust. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Connect from a personal device to a virtual privileged workstation and administer from there
Publish RDP on the management servers to an allow list of home IP addresses
Connect from the privileged access workstation through a hardened remote access intermediary
Use the standard corporate laptop with a separate administrator account

explanation: The administrator should start from the privileged access workstation and reach the servers through a hardened intermediary such as a bastion or dedicated privileged remote access service, so every hop is trusted. Connecting from a personal device into a privileged virtual machine lets a lower-trust device control the session. Publishing RDP exposes management ports to the internet, and a separate account on a standard laptop still exposes privileged credentials on a device used for email and browsing.

prompt: After an intrusion, a company believes the attacker extracted the krbtgt account hash from a domain controller and can forge Kerberos tickets. Which action should the architect include in the recovery plan to invalidate the forged tickets?

options.text: Reset the password of every Domain Admins member once
Reset the krbtgt password twice, with an interval between the resets
Restart all domain controllers in the affected domain
Raise the domain and forest functional levels

explanation: Forged ticket-granting tickets are signed with the krbtgt key, and because the current and previous keys are both accepted, the password must be reset twice with time between the resets to invalidate them. Resetting administrator passwords does not change the krbtgt key. Restarting domain controllers and raising functional levels do not invalidate tickets signed with the stolen key.

prompt: A company wants to evaluate and monitor its on-premises Active Directory Domain Services for attacks such as pass-the-hash and directory replication abuse, and to receive posture assessments on weaknesses such as unsecure Kerberos delegation. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Entra Connect Health
Microsoft Defender for Identity

explanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity uses sensors on domain controllers and other identity servers to detect attacks against Active Directory and provides identity security posture assessments. Entra ID Protection evaluates risk for cloud sign-ins and users. Defender for Cloud Apps monitors cloud application activity, and Entra Connect Health reports the health of synchronisation and federation services rather than detecting attacks.

prompt: An evaluation of a company's Active Directory Domain Services finds service accounts that have service principal names, passwords set years ago and membership of privileged groups. This exposes the domain to Kerberoasting. Which recommendation addresses the weakness?

options.text: Move services to group managed service accounts with least privilege
Add the service accounts to the Protected Users group
Set the accounts to never expire and require 14-character passwords
Give the accounts Domain Admins membership to simplify delegation

explanation: Group managed service accounts have long, random passwords that the directory changes automatically, which makes offline cracking of their service tickets impractical, and least privilege limits the damage if one is compromised. Microsoft advises against adding service accounts to Protected Users, because its restrictions break service authentication. A static 14-character password remains crackable, and Domain Admins membership increases the impact of a compromise.

prompt: A company's Global Administrator roles are assigned to accounts that are synchronised from on-premises Active Directory. The architect must ensure that a compromise of the on-premises directory cannot be used to take over the cloud tenant. What should be recommended?

options.text: Keep the synchronised accounts and enable password hash synchronization
Federate the administrator accounts through the existing AD FS farm
Use cloud-only administrator accounts with phishing-resistant authentication
Use one shared administrator account whose password is kept in a safe

explanation: Privileged cloud roles should be held by cloud-only accounts so that control of the on-premises directory does not give control of those identities, and phishing-resistant authentication protects the accounts themselves. Synchronised or federated administrator accounts can be manipulated by anyone who controls the on-premises directory or the federation servers. A shared account removes individual accountability.

prompt: An architect is designing emergency access to a Microsoft Entra tenant for use when normal administrator sign-in fails, for example during a Conditional Access misconfiguration or an outage of the MFA service. Which design should be recommended?

options.text: One synchronised account whose password is split between two safes in the on-premises datacenter
Two cloud-only accounts excluded from Conditional Access, with alerts on any sign-in
Emergency accounts that are subject to every Conditional Access policy
A service principal with a client secret and the Global Administrator role

explanation: Emergency access accounts should be cloud-only, kept out of the Conditional Access policies that could lock administrators out, strongly protected and monitored so that any use raises an alert. A synchronised account depends on on-premises infrastructure that might be the cause of the outage. Accounts subject to every policy would be locked out by the same misconfiguration, and a service principal secret is a long-lived credential that is not intended for interactive recovery.

prompt: A company runs workloads in Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. The architect must design a way to find identities that hold permissions they do not use across all three clouds, and to produce recommendations for reducing those permissions. Which solution should be recommended?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Microsoft Entra access reviews
App governance policies for OAuth applications in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
CIEM capabilities in the Defender CSPM plan of Defender for Cloud

explanation: Cloud infrastructure entitlement management in Defender for Cloud, part of the Defender CSPM plan, analyses the permissions and activity of identities in Azure, AWS and Google Cloud and recommends removing excess. Privileged Identity Management provides just-in-time activation for Microsoft Entra and Azure roles but does not analyse permission use in AWS or Google Cloud. Access reviews ask people to attest to access, and app governance monitors OAuth applications rather than cloud infrastructure entitlements.

prompt: An architect is specifying the privileged access workstation solution for administrators of a company's identity systems. Which two requirements should be included? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use a dedicated hardened device for administrative tasks only
Require the privileged workstation, through Conditional Access, for administrative portals
Allow the workstation to be reached by RDP from the administrator's daily-use laptop
Install email and collaboration apps on the workstation to reduce the device count

explanation: A privileged access workstation is a dedicated, hardened device reserved for sensitive administration, and Conditional Access should enforce that privileged roles can reach administrative portals only from it. Reaching the workstation by RDP from a daily-use laptop lets a lower-trust device control privileged sessions. Email and collaboration apps bring the main phishing and malware entry points onto the device.

prompt: A compliance requirement states that data at rest must be encrypted with keys that the organisation itself controls and can revoke at any time. Which security control should the architect specify for the company's Azure storage accounts and databases?

options.text: Encryption with platform-managed keys
Encryption with customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault
A minimum TLS version of 1.2 on every endpoint
Azure DDoS Protection on the virtual networks

explanation: Customer-managed keys held in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM let the organisation control the key lifecycle and revoke access to the data by disabling the key. Platform-managed keys encrypt the data, but Microsoft controls them. A minimum TLS version protects data in transit, and DDoS Protection addresses availability, so neither satisfies a requirement about key control at rest.

prompt: A regulation requires that all of a company's Azure resources are created only in European Union regions. The control must prevent non-compliant deployments in every current and future subscription. How should the architect translate this requirement into a control?

options.text: A mandatory Region tag on every resource group
Network security group rules that block traffic to and from non-EU address ranges
A Defender for Cloud alert on deployments outside the EU
An allowed locations policy with the deny effect at management group scope

explanation: An Azure Policy assignment that restricts allowed locations with the deny effect blocks deployments to other regions, and assigning it at a management group covers subscriptions added later. A tag records an intended region but enforces nothing. Network security group rules filter traffic rather than control where resources are created, and an alert is raised only after the non-compliant resource exists.

prompt: A payment card standard requires that systems which store cardholder data are segmented from the rest of the environment, so that the scope of assessment is limited. Which control design should the architect specify in Azure?

options.text: A dedicated subscription and isolated network for the cardholder systems, with filtered traffic
A CardholderData tag applied to every resource that stores card numbers, with a cost and inventory report
Disk encryption with platform-managed keys on the cardholder systems
The Reader role for the assessors on the existing shared subscription

explanation: Segmentation is achieved by isolating the cardholder data environment, for example in its own subscription and virtual network with traffic controlled by a firewall and network security groups. Tags label resources without separating them. Disk encryption protects stored data but does not reduce connectivity or scope, and giving assessors read access leaves the systems in a shared environment.

prompt: During an ISO/IEC 27001 audit, a company is asked for evidence of the physical security controls of the datacenters that host its Azure workloads. Under the shared responsibility model, how should the architect address this control?

options.text: Request an on-site inspection of the Azure datacenters by the auditor
Assign an Azure Policy initiative to the physical host servers
Use Microsoft's independent audit reports from the Service Trust Portal
Run a Defender for Cloud vulnerability scan of the datacenter

explanation: Physical datacenter security is Microsoft's responsibility, and customers inherit that control by relying on the independent audit reports and certifications that Microsoft publishes in the Service Trust Portal. Customers cannot arrange their own on-site inspections of Azure datacenters. Azure Policy and Defender for Cloud assess the customer's own resources, not Microsoft's physical facilities.

prompt: A compliance team needs to track its Microsoft 365 environment against GDPR and ISO/IEC 27001, assign recommended actions to owners, attach evidence and report an overall score to management. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Secure Score
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Microsoft Purview Audit
Microsoft Defender XDR reports

explanation: Compliance Manager provides assessments built from regulatory templates, improvement actions that can be assigned and evidenced, and a compliance score. Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture and is not organised by regulation. Purview Audit records user and administrator activity, and Defender XDR reports cover threats and protection status rather than regulatory assessments.

prompt: A regulator requires that certain financial documents in SharePoint are kept for seven years, and that during that period nobody, including administrators, can delete them or remove the retention marking. Which Microsoft Purview design should the architect recommend?

options.text: A sensitivity label that applies encryption
A data loss prevention policy for financial data
A retention policy applied to all SharePoint sites
A retention label that marks items as regulatory records

explanation: A retention label that marks content as a regulatory record prevents deletion and prevents the label from being removed, even by administrators, for the retention period. A sensitivity label controls access and encryption, and a data loss prevention policy controls sharing, so neither enforces retention. A retention policy keeps a copy of content, but administrators can change or remove the policy and it does not declare items as immutable records.

prompt: To meet a payment card requirement, a company must prevent users from sending credit card numbers to external recipients through Exchange Online, Teams chats and SharePoint sharing. Which Microsoft Purview solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Data loss prevention policies
Retention labels and policies
eDiscovery cases with holds
Insider Risk Management policies

explanation: Data loss prevention policies detect sensitive information types such as credit card numbers and can block or restrict sharing across Exchange, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. Retention labels govern how long content is kept, and eDiscovery finds and preserves content for legal matters. Insider Risk Management identifies risky user behaviour for investigation rather than blocking each sharing attempt.

prompt: A financial regulator requires a brokerage to supervise traders' email and Teams messages for signs of market manipulation, with flagged messages sent to compliance reviewers. Which Microsoft Purview solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Data loss prevention
Information Barriers
Communication Compliance
eDiscovery

explanation: Communication Compliance detects potentially inappropriate or regulated messages in channels such as email and Teams and routes them to designated reviewers. Data loss prevention blocks sharing of sensitive information types rather than supervising conduct. Information Barriers prevent defined groups from communicating at all, and eDiscovery searches and preserves content for legal cases after the fact.

prompt: To avoid conflicts of interest, a regulation requires that an investment bank's research analysts and its advisory bankers cannot chat, call or share files with each other in Microsoft Teams and SharePoint. Which Microsoft Purview solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Communication Compliance
Information Barriers
Sensitivity labels
Customer Lockbox

explanation: Information Barriers policies stop defined segments of users from communicating and collaborating with each other in Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. Communication Compliance reviews messages after they are sent and does not prevent contact. Sensitivity labels protect individual items, and Customer Lockbox controls Microsoft support engineers' access to customer content.

prompt: A compliance requirement states that Microsoft engineers must not access a company's Microsoft 365 content during a support case unless the company explicitly approves each request. Which capability should the architect include in the design?

options.text: Customer Key
Double Key Encryption
Privileged access management
Customer Lockbox

explanation: Customer Lockbox requires the customer's approval before a Microsoft engineer can access customer content during a support operation. Customer Key gives the organisation control over the root encryption keys for data at rest, and Double Key Encryption protects selected highly sensitive items with a second key held by the customer. Privileged access management in Microsoft 365 controls the organisation's own administrators' privileged tasks.

prompt: A company is told to expect litigation. Its legal team must preserve the mailboxes and OneDrive content of 12 named employees, then search, review and export the relevant items. Which Microsoft Purview solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: eDiscovery cases with custodian holds
An organisation-wide retention policy
A data loss prevention policy
Audit log retention policies

explanation: eDiscovery cases let the legal team place holds on specific custodians' data sources and then search, review and export the content. An organisation-wide retention policy keeps everything for everyone and provides no case workflow. Data loss prevention controls sharing of sensitive data, and audit log retention policies determine how long activity records are kept rather than preserving content.

prompt: A compliance standard requires every Azure key vault to send its diagnostic logs to a central Log Analytics workspace. The design must configure this automatically for new vaults and bring existing vaults into compliance. Which Azure Policy design should the architect recommend?

options.text: A policy with the audit effect and a monthly compliance report
A policy with the deny effect for vaults without diagnostic settings
A deployIfNotExists policy with a managed identity and a remediation task
A policy with the manual effect and quarterly attestations from the vault owners

explanation: The deployIfNotExists effect deploys the diagnostic setting when it is missing by using the assignment's managed identity, and a remediation task applies it to existing resources. The audit effect only reports non-compliance. The deny effect cannot bring existing vaults into compliance and does not create the setting, and the manual effect records attestations without configuring anything.

prompt: A compliance requirement states that production Log Analytics workspaces must not be deleted. The control must be assigned at management group scope, and subscription owners must not be able to remove it. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: A CanNotDelete resource lock on each workspace
An Azure Policy assignment that uses the denyAction effect
An Azure Policy assignment that uses the deny effect
An Azure Policy assignment that uses the auditIfNotExists effect

explanation: The denyAction effect blocks specified actions, such as delete, on resources in scope, and an assignment at a management group cannot be removed by someone who only owns a subscription beneath it. A subscription owner can remove a CanNotDelete lock. The deny effect evaluates create and update requests rather than deletions, and auditIfNotExists only reports on missing related resources.

prompt: A company must demonstrate alignment with a regulatory standard that maps to more than 100 Azure Policy definitions. The architect wants to assign and track them as one unit across all subscriptions. Which design should be recommended?

options.text: Each definition assigned separately to each subscription
A custom Azure role that includes the required permissions
A set of saved Azure Resource Graph queries
The standard's policy initiative assigned at a management group

explanation: An initiative groups related policy definitions so they can be assigned once and reported together, and assigning it at a management group covers every subscription below. Assigning each definition to each subscription is hard to maintain and report on. A custom role controls who may perform actions rather than how resources are configured, and Resource Graph queries can report on resources but do not evaluate or enforce policy.

prompt: A legacy application cannot meet one policy in a compliance initiative for the next six months, and a compensating control is in place. The exception must be documented, must end automatically and must remain visible in compliance reporting. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: A policy exemption in the Mitigated category with an expiry date
An excluded scope added to the initiative assignment
A change of the policy effect to Disabled in the assignment
Removal of the initiative from the application's subscription

explanation: A policy exemption records why a resource is exempt, the Mitigated category shows that the intent is met by another control, and an expiry date ends the exemption automatically while it stays visible in reporting. An excluded scope removes the resource from evaluation with no category or expiry. Disabling the effect or removing the initiative switches the control off for every resource in scope, not only for the legacy application.

prompt: A company has workloads in Azure subscriptions and AWS accounts that are connected to Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Auditors want one place that shows how the resources in both clouds align with PCI DSS. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Secure Score in the Microsoft Defender portal
Azure Advisor security recommendations
The PCI DSS standard assigned in Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance
A Microsoft Sentinel workbook built on the Azure and AWS activity logs of both clouds

explanation: Regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud lets standards be assigned to Azure subscriptions and to connected AWS accounts and GCP projects, and its dashboard shows the status of each control. Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal covers Microsoft 365 and identity settings. Azure Advisor is limited to Azure and is not organised by regulatory control, and an activity log workbook shows operations rather than control compliance.

prompt: A company uses only the free foundational posture capabilities of Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and its dashboard shows the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark. The compliance team now wants its subscriptions evaluated against ISO/IEC 27001 in the regulatory compliance dashboard. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Assign the standard directly, because all standards are included at no cost
Enable a qualifying Defender for Cloud plan, then assign the standard
Buy Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences for the compliance team
Deploy Microsoft Sentinel and install a compliance solution

explanation: The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark is assessed by default, but adding other regulatory standards requires a paid Defender for Cloud plan on the scope, after which the standard can be assigned. The additional standards are not part of the free foundational capabilities. Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences and Microsoft Sentinel are not prerequisites for the regulatory compliance dashboard.

prompt: A company runs workloads in Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. The security architect wants one security standard that Microsoft Defender for Cloud assesses by default across all three clouds, without buying a paid plan. Which approach meets the requirement?

options.text: Rely on the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark that Foundational CSPM applies to connected environments
Build an assessment for each cloud in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Enable Defender CSPM and add a separate regulatory standard for each cloud provider
Author a custom Azure Policy initiative and assign it to the AWS and GCP connectors

explanation: Foundational CSPM is free and applies the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) to connected Azure, AWS and GCP environments, producing recommendations and a secure score. Enabling Defender CSPM with extra regulatory standards works but is a paid plan. Compliance Manager assessments track regulatory improvement actions rather than continuously assessing cloud resources for Defender for Cloud. Azure Policy initiatives evaluate Azure resources and cannot be assigned to AWS or GCP connectors as the default multicloud standard.

prompt: One virtual machine fails a Defender for Cloud recommendation, but the risk is already mitigated by a third-party control. The architect wants that single resource to stop counting against the secure score, with a recorded justification, while every other resource stays assessed. What should be recommended?

options.text: Create an exemption for the resource with a mitigated justification
Assign a governance rule that gives the owner a long grace period
Change the built-in policy effect for the recommendation to Deny
Disable the recommendation in the security policy of the subscription

explanation: An exemption scopes out one resource (or a scope) from a recommendation, records the justification and removes it from the secure score calculation. Disabling the recommendation in the subscription's security policy stops assessment of every resource, not just the one. A governance rule with a grace period only postpones the impact and still expects remediation. A Deny effect blocks new non-compliant deployments and does nothing for the existing mitigated resource.

prompt: A security team uses Foundational CSPM in Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Which TWO capabilities would require them to enable the Defender CSPM plan? (Choose two.)

options.text: Workflow automation
Risk hunting with the cloud security explorer
Asset inventory
Secure score
Attack path analysis

explanation: Attack path analysis and the cloud security explorer are built on the cloud security graph, which is available only in the paid Defender CSPM plan. Secure score, asset inventory and workflow automation are all included in the free Foundational CSPM plan.

prompt: Hundreds of open Defender for Cloud recommendations have no clear owner. The CISO wants each recommendation automatically assigned to a resource owner with a due date, and wants overdue items tracked. Which capability should the architect include in the design?

options.text: Workflow automation with a Logic App
Governance rules in Defender CSPM
Azure Policy remediation tasks
Recommendation exemptions with an expiry date

explanation: Governance rules assign owners and remediation time frames to recommendations at scale and report on overdue items; they are part of Defender CSPM. Workflow automation can trigger a Logic App but does not provide built-in ownership and due-date tracking. Azure Policy remediation tasks fix resources for deployIfNotExists or modify policies and assign nobody. Exemptions remove resources from assessment instead of driving remediation.

prompt: An organization has an AWS organization with 60 member accounts, and new accounts are created every month. The architect must bring all accounts under Defender for Cloud posture management with the least ongoing administration. What should be recommended?

options.text: Create one connector for the AWS management account and onboard member accounts automatically
Stream AWS CloudTrail logs to Microsoft Sentinel by using the Amazon S3 connector
Install the Azure Connected Machine agent on every EC2 instance in each account
Create a separate Defender for Cloud connector for each AWS member account

explanation: Onboarding the AWS management account lets Defender for Cloud discover the member accounts and automatically onboard existing and newly created ones. A connector per member account works but must be repeated for every new account. Installing the Connected Machine agent covers only EC2 servers and gives no posture assessment of AWS services. Sending CloudTrail logs to Sentinel supports detection and hunting, not security posture recommendations.

prompt: A company runs containerized applications on Amazon EKS and Google GKE. It requires image vulnerability assessment and runtime threat detection for the clusters, with alerts available in Microsoft Defender XDR. Which Defender for Cloud plan should the architect select?

options.text: Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender for Containers
Defender for App Service
Foundational CSPM

explanation: Defender for Containers provides vulnerability assessment for images and runtime threat protection for Kubernetes clusters in Azure, AWS and GCP, and its alerts flow to Defender XDR. Defender for Servers Plan 2 protects machines as servers and has no Kubernetes-aware detections. Defender for App Service protects Azure App Service only. Foundational CSPM gives recommendations and secure score but no runtime threat detection.

prompt: A subscription contains 500 virtual machines. Only 40 of them need endpoint detection and response with agent-based vulnerability scanning, and the budget does not allow any other server protection to be purchased. Which recommendation meets the requirement at the lowest cost?

options.text: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 on the subscription for all machines
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 at the resource level on the 40 machines
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 at the resource level on the 40 machines
Enable Defender CSPM on the subscription and use agentless scanning

explanation: Defender for Servers Plan 1 delivers Defender for Endpoint EDR and agent-based vulnerability scanning, and it can be enabled per resource. Plan 2 cannot be enabled at the resource level; it can only be disabled per resource after subscription-level enablement, and it costs more. Enabling Plan 1 on the whole subscription pays for 460 machines that do not need it. Defender CSPM provides posture features and agentless scanning but not EDR.

prompt: A manufacturer has Windows and Linux servers in its own datacenters. The servers must appear in Defender for Cloud, be protected by Defender for Servers, and be governed by Azure Policy, without migrating them to Azure. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy the Azure Migrate appliance and discover the servers
Replicate the servers with Azure Site Recovery
Onboard the servers as Azure Arc-enabled servers
Register the servers through a Log Analytics gateway

explanation: Azure Arc-enabled servers project on-premises machines into Azure Resource Manager, so Defender for Cloud plans, Azure Policy and extensions can be applied to them in place. Azure Migrate discovers and assesses servers for migration but does not make them manageable Azure resources. Azure Site Recovery replicates machines for disaster recovery. A Log Analytics gateway only proxies log traffic and does not onboard machines to Defender for Cloud.

prompt: A retailer operates Kubernetes clusters in its stores on its own hardware. The architect must extend Defender for Containers threat detection and Azure Policy for Kubernetes to these clusters. Which design should be used?

options.text: Onboard each cluster node as an Azure Arc-enabled server
Connect the clusters to Azure as Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes
Manage the stores' subscriptions through Azure Lighthouse
Push the store images to a connected registry of Azure Container Registry

explanation: Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes represents on-premises clusters in Azure so that cluster extensions such as the Defender sensor and Azure Policy for Kubernetes can be deployed. Arc-enabling each node as a server manages the operating system but gives no Kubernetes-level protection or policy. Azure Lighthouse delegates management of Azure resources across tenants and connects nothing on-premises. A connected registry only synchronizes images to the edge.

prompt: An architect plans to onboard 3,000 on-premises servers to Azure Arc with a scripted, non-interactive deployment. The credential embedded in the script must follow least privilege. Which identity should the script use?

options.text: A break-glass Global Administrator account with a long random password
A service principal that holds only the Azure Connected Machine Onboarding role
A service principal that holds the Contributor role on the subscription
A system-assigned managed identity of each on-premises server

explanation: A service principal limited to the Azure Connected Machine Onboarding role can only onboard machines, which is the recommended approach for at-scale scripted onboarding. A Contributor service principal works but grants far more than onboarding requires. On-premises servers have no managed identity until after they are Arc-enabled, so it cannot be used to onboard them. A Global Administrator account is highly privileged, interactive in nature and must never be embedded in scripts.

prompt: After several acquisitions, a company suspects that forgotten domains, hosts and web applications exist on the internet under its name. The architect needs continuous outside-in discovery of these assets without deploying agents or supplying credentials. Which solution should be recommended?

options.text: Agentless machine scanning in Defender for Servers Plan 2
Microsoft Sentinel user and entity behavior analytics
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management

explanation: Defender EASM continuously discovers and maps internet-facing assets such as domains, hosts, IP blocks and ASNs from the outside, with no agents or credentials. Defender Vulnerability Management assesses devices that are already onboarded or discovered on the internal network. Agentless scanning in Defender for Servers examines disks of known cloud VMs in connected subscriptions. Sentinel UEBA analyses the behavior of users and entities in collected logs.

prompt: A company already uses Defender EASM for its own brand. It acquires a competitor and must add the competitor's unknown internet-facing infrastructure to the inventory. What should the architect recommend as the first step?

options.text: Deploy network scanning appliances in the acquired company's datacenters
Create a discovery group that uses the acquired company's known domains and other assets as seeds
Import the acquired company's configuration management database as approved inventory
Connect the acquired company's Azure subscriptions to Defender for Cloud

explanation: Defender EASM discovery starts from seeds, which are known legitimate assets such as domains, IP blocks or ASNs, and recursively finds connected infrastructure; a custom discovery group with the acquired company's seeds extends the inventory. Scanning appliances inside datacenters give an internal view and are not how EASM works. Connecting Azure subscriptions reveals only assets hosted in those subscriptions. A CMDB lists what is already known, which is the opposite of discovering unknown assets.

prompt: A security team has capacity to fix only a few issues this quarter. Using Microsoft Security Exposure Management, the architect must specify what to remediate first so that the largest number of routes to critical assets is cut. What should be prioritized?

options.text: Recommended actions that add the most Secure Score points
Devices with the largest number of high CVSS vulnerabilities
Choke points that many attack paths pass through
Assets that generated the most alerts in the last 30 days

explanation: Choke points are assets where many attack paths converge, so fixing them breaks the most paths to critical assets for the least effort. Ranking devices by CVSS count ignores whether the device is actually on a route to anything critical. Chasing Secure Score points improves general hygiene but is not tied to attack paths. Alert volume reflects past detections and not exposure.

prompt: The CISO wants to run a ransomware-readiness program and track it in Microsoft Security Exposure Management with a score, underlying metrics and progress over time. Which capability should the architect specify?

options.text: The attack surface map
Custom detection rules in advanced hunting
Security initiatives
Threat analytics reports

explanation: Security initiatives group metrics and recommendations for a security domain or threat, such as ransomware protection, and show a score that can be tracked over time. The attack surface map visualizes assets and their connections but does not score a program. Custom detection rules raise alerts from hunting queries. Threat analytics reports describe threats and affected assets but are not a managed posture program with targets.

prompt: An organization wants attack path prioritization in Microsoft Security Exposure Management to treat its payment processing servers as high-value targets, in addition to assets that Microsoft already recognizes such as domain controllers. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Create a custom critical asset classification that matches the payment servers
Add the payment servers to a Microsoft Sentinel watchlist
Place the payment servers in a device group with full automated remediation
Apply a device tag to the payment servers in Defender for Endpoint

explanation: Critical asset management has predefined classifications and lets you create custom ones; assets marked critical are used to prioritize attack paths and recommendations. A device tag by itself only labels the device and does not change criticality. A device group controls access and automation level for remediation. A Sentinel watchlist enriches analytics rules and is not consumed by exposure management.

prompt: A company enforces multifactor authentication through a non-Microsoft identity provider. In Microsoft Secure Score the related MFA recommended action is still open, and leadership wants the score to reflect the real posture. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Set the action status to Resolved through third party
Set the action status to Risk accepted
Remove the identity category from the Secure Score view
Add a duplicate Conditional Access policy that requires Microsoft Entra MFA

explanation: Marking a recommended action as Resolved through third party records that another product covers the control and awards the points. Risk accepted documents that the risk is tolerated and gives no points, which misrepresents a control that is actually in place. Adding a duplicate Microsoft Entra MFA requirement forces users to perform MFA twice just to change a metric. Filtering out the identity category hides the gap from a view without changing the score.

prompt: An architect is preparing a board report and needs to show how the organization's Microsoft 365 security configuration posture compares with organizations of similar size and industry. Which metric source should be used?

options.text: The regulatory compliance dashboard in Defender for Cloud
The device exposure score in Defender Vulnerability Management
The compliance score in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
The comparison data in Microsoft Secure Score

explanation: Microsoft Secure Score includes a comparison of your score with organizations like yours, which directly supports peer benchmarking of security configuration posture. The Compliance Manager score measures progress on regulatory improvement actions. The Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard assesses cloud resources against standards. The device exposure score reflects endpoint vulnerability exposure only.

prompt: A company has Windows and Linux servers in Azure, AWS and its own datacenter. Defender for Servers Plan 2 must assess operating system settings on all of them against the compute security baselines of the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark. Which requirement should the architect specify?

options.text: Apply the Security Compliance Toolkit baselines through Group Policy on every server
Arc-enable the non-Azure servers and run the Azure machine configuration extension on every server
Enroll every server in Microsoft Intune and assign a security baseline profile
Install the Log Analytics agent on every server and link it to a central workspace

explanation: OS baseline assessment in Defender for Cloud relies on the Azure machine configuration extension, and machines outside Azure must be onboarded with Azure Arc to run it. The Log Analytics agent is no longer used for this feature. Intune security baselines target client devices and do not feed Defender for Cloud recommendations. Security Compliance Toolkit GPOs configure Windows only and give no assessment of Linux or reporting in Defender for Cloud.

prompt: Administrators manage Azure virtual machines over RDP and SSH. The requirement is that management ports stay closed in the network security groups until an approved request opens them for a limited time and only for the requester's source IP address. Which solution should the architect specify?

options.text: A network security group rule that allows the corporate public IP range
Azure Bastion Basic deployed in the hub virtual network
Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers Plan 2
Privileged Identity Management for the Virtual Machine Contributor role

explanation: Just-in-time VM access keeps management ports blocked and adds a time-bound NSG allow rule scoped to the requester's IP when a request is approved. PIM makes an Azure role assignment time-bound but does not open or close network ports. A static NSG rule for the corporate range leaves the ports permanently open to that range. Azure Bastion brokers the session without a public IP on the VM, but by itself it does not provide request-based, time-limited port opening.

prompt: Latency-sensitive trading servers may not have any additional security agent installed. The company still requires software inventory, vulnerability assessment and discovery of secrets stored on the server disks. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Update Manager periodic assessment
Agentless machine scanning in Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender for Endpoint onboarding through Defender for Servers Plan 1
A network vulnerability scanner that probes the servers every night

explanation: Agentless scanning in Defender for Servers Plan 2 analyses disk snapshots out of band, providing software inventory, vulnerability findings and secrets scanning with no agent and no performance impact on the server. Plan 1 depends on the Defender for Endpoint agent, which violates the no-agent constraint. Azure Update Manager reports missing updates only. A nightly network scanner adds load to the servers and cannot find secrets stored on disk.

prompt: A security review finds that phishing documents on Windows clients launch child processes from Office applications and attempt to read credentials from the LSASS process. Which control should the architect specify to block these behaviors?

options.text: Controlled folder access
BitLocker with TPM and PIN
Microsoft Defender SmartScreen
Attack surface reduction rules

explanation: Attack surface reduction rules include rules that block Office applications from creating child processes and block credential stealing from LSASS. Controlled folder access protects files in designated folders from untrusted applications, which is a ransomware control. SmartScreen warns about or blocks malicious sites and downloads based on reputation. BitLocker protects data at rest when a device is lost or stolen.

prompt: Privileged access workstations must run only software that the organization has explicitly authorized, including kernel drivers, and the restriction must hold even against a user with local administrator rights. Which technology should the architect specify?

options.text: Controlled folder access
Attack surface reduction rules
Exploit protection settings
App Control for Business policies

explanation: App Control for Business (formerly Windows Defender Application Control) enforces an allow list of trusted code in both user and kernel mode and is designed to resist tampering by local administrators. Attack surface reduction rules block specific risky behaviors but do not create an allow list of software. Controlled folder access only limits which apps can write to protected folders. Exploit protection applies memory mitigations to processes.

prompt: Employees use personal iOS and Android phones for Outlook and Teams. The company may not enroll these devices, but corporate data must require an app PIN, must not be copied into personal apps, and must be removable without touching personal content. What should the architect specify?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy that requires a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Intune app protection policies enforced with a Conditional Access grant that requires them
Microsoft Purview endpoint data loss prevention policies for the phones
Intune device compliance policies enforced with a compliant-device Conditional Access grant

explanation: App protection policies (MAM) secure corporate data inside managed apps on unenrolled devices, with PIN, copy/paste restrictions and selective wipe, and Conditional Access can require an app protection policy. Compliance policies with a compliant-device grant require the device to be enrolled. Hybrid join applies to domain-joined Windows devices, not phones. Endpoint DLP protects onboarded Windows and macOS devices rather than iOS and Android.

prompt: A company manages iOS and Android devices with Intune. It wants phishing links, malicious apps and jailbroken or rooted devices to be detected on the phones, and wants access to Microsoft 365 blocked while a device is at elevated risk. Which design should the architect specify?

options.text: Defender for Endpoint on the phones, with its device risk level used in Intune compliance policies
Intune device restriction profiles that block all app store installations
Intune app configuration policies that set a managed browser for all links
Sign-in risk policies in Microsoft Entra ID Protection for mobile users

explanation: Defender for Endpoint on iOS and Android acts as mobile threat defense, and Intune compliance policies can mark a device non-compliant above a chosen threat level so that Conditional Access blocks it. App configuration policies only preconfigure app settings and detect nothing. Sign-in risk evaluates the authentication, not threats on the device. Blocking app stores removes one infection route but detects neither phishing nor compromised devices and provides no risk signal.

prompt: A device maker ships thousands of sensors that must connect to Azure IoT Hub. The requirement is zero-touch onboarding with a unique, hardware-backed identity per device and no shared secret stored in the firmware image. What should the architect specify?

options.text: Manual registration of each device with a connection string emailed to the installer
A single IoT Hub shared access policy key compiled into the firmware
One group symmetric key that every device uses to derive its credentials at first boot
IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service with X.509 certificate or TPM attestation

explanation: The Device Provisioning Service registers devices automatically and supports X.509 certificate and TPM attestation, giving each device its own hardware-rooted identity. A shared access policy key in firmware gives every device the same hub-level credential, so one extracted image compromises all. A group symmetric key is still a shared secret embedded in every device. Manual registration with emailed connection strings does not scale and exposes secrets in transit.

prompt: Corporate offices contain printers, cameras and VoIP phones that cannot run an agent. Windows endpoints on the same networks are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. The architect must gain an inventory of the unmanaged devices and their vulnerabilities with the least new infrastructure. What should be recommended?

options.text: Device discovery in Defender for Endpoint with enterprise IoT security
Enrollment of the devices in Microsoft Intune
Azure Arc onboarding of each printer, camera and phone
Defender for Servers Plan 1 on the office subscriptions

explanation: Onboarded Defender for Endpoint devices can discover unmanaged devices on their networks, and enterprise IoT security adds vulnerability and recommendation data for printers, cameras and similar devices without new sensors. Intune enrollment requires a supported operating system and management client that these devices lack. Defender for Servers protects server operating systems. Azure Arc requires the Connected Machine agent, which cannot run on such devices.

prompt: A chemical plant must monitor its PLCs and engineering workstations for threats. The controllers cannot run security software, and the solution must not inject traffic into the process network. Which solution should the architect recommend?

options.text: Azure Firewall Premium with IDPS placed inline between the PLCs
The Defender for Endpoint agent deployed to the PLCs and workstations
A Defender for IoT OT network sensor connected to a SPAN port or network TAP
Authenticated active scans from Defender Vulnerability Management

explanation: Defender for IoT OT sensors passively analyse mirrored traffic from a SPAN port or TAP with OT-aware deep packet inspection, so nothing is installed on controllers and no traffic is injected. PLCs cannot run the Defender for Endpoint agent. Authenticated active scanning sends traffic to fragile controllers, which the requirement forbids. Azure Firewall is a cloud network service and cannot sit inline inside a plant control network.

prompt: A power utility's policy states that its substation control networks may never have any connection to the internet or to cloud services. The utility still wants Defender for IoT monitoring at each substation. Which deployment should the architect specify?

options.text: Enterprise IoT discovery through Defender for Endpoint devices in each substation
OT sensors that forward all alerts directly to the Microsoft Sentinel connector
Cloud-connected OT sensors that reach Azure through an outbound proxy
Locally managed OT sensors with threat intelligence packages uploaded manually

explanation: OT sensors can run fully on-premises as locally managed sensors; data is viewed in the sensor console and threat intelligence packages are uploaded by hand. Cloud-connected sensors, even through a proxy, create the cloud connection the policy prohibits. Forwarding alerts to the Sentinel connector also needs cloud connectivity. Enterprise IoT discovery depends on Defender for Endpoint cloud services and is not designed for OT process networks.

prompt: A manufacturer's SOC uses Microsoft Sentinel for IT incidents. It wants alerts about its plant floor devices to appear in the same queue so that analysts can correlate IT and OT activity. Which design should the architect recommend?

options.text: Syslog forwarding configured directly on every PLC to a Log Analytics workspace
Intune compliance reports for the engineering workstations exported to Sentinel
Cloud-connected OT sensors with the Defender for IoT solution and data connector in Sentinel
Locally managed OT sensors that analysts review in each sensor console

explanation: Cloud-connected sensors deliver alert information to Defender for IoT in Azure, and the Sentinel data connector and solution bring those alerts into Sentinel for correlation with IT data. Locally managed sensors keep data in separate consoles, which prevents a single queue. PLCs generally cannot forward security-relevant syslog and this would bypass OT-aware analytics. Intune compliance reports cover managed workstations only and contain no OT threat detections.

prompt: A company manages Windows 11 devices with Microsoft Intune. The architect must specify how Microsoft-recommended security settings are applied to the devices as a versioned, preconfigured group of settings that can be adjusted where necessary. What should be specified?

options.text: Intune security baselines
Security Compliance Toolkit GPO backups
Intune device compliance policies
Intune update rings for Windows

explanation: Intune security baselines are versioned, preconfigured groups of settings that apply Microsoft's recommended security configuration and can be customized. Compliance policies evaluate whether a device meets rules but do not configure the settings. Security Compliance Toolkit GPO backups are meant for Group Policy in Active Directory, not Intune-managed devices. Update rings control when Windows updates install.

prompt: An organization manages its Windows Server estate only through Active Directory Group Policy. The architect must specify how the team obtains Microsoft-recommended baseline GPOs and compares them with the GPOs currently in production. Which tool set should be specified?

options.text: Intune security baselines with per-setting status reports
Microsoft Secure Score recommended actions
Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit with Policy Analyzer
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager assessments

explanation: The Security Compliance Toolkit provides Microsoft's recommended baselines as GPO backups, and its Policy Analyzer compares sets of GPOs to reveal differences and conflicts. Intune security baselines need Intune-managed devices, which this estate does not use. Secure Score recommends tenant and product configuration changes rather than server GPO baselines. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory improvement actions.

prompt: Auditors require evidence that Windows endpoints are continuously measured against CIS and STIG benchmarks. The endpoints are already onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, and the evidence should come from the Microsoft Defender portal. What should the architect specify?

options.text: Intune security baseline profiles with the default Microsoft settings
Attack surface reduction rule reports in the Defender portal
Device configuration recommendations in Microsoft Secure Score
Security baselines assessment in Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

explanation: Security baselines assessment in Defender Vulnerability Management continuously evaluates onboarded devices against industry benchmarks such as CIS and STIG and reports compliance per profile. Intune security baselines apply Microsoft's own recommended settings and do not measure CIS or STIG benchmarks. Secure Score recommendations are not benchmark compliance evidence. Attack surface reduction reports cover only those rules.

prompt: A company's Windows 11 devices are Microsoft Entra hybrid joined. A proposed design backs up each device's Windows LAPS password to both Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID for redundancy. How should the architect evaluate the proposal?

options.text: It is valid, provided that the Active Directory schema is extended for Windows LAPS first
It is not possible; hybrid joined devices can back up passwords only to Active Directory
It is not possible; a hybrid joined device backs up to one directory, so one must be chosen
It is valid, because hybrid joined devices always write the password to both directories

explanation: Windows LAPS on a hybrid joined device can back up the password either to Microsoft Entra ID or to Windows Server Active Directory, but never to both. The claim that hybrid devices always write to both is therefore wrong. Hybrid joined devices are not limited to Active Directory; Entra ID is an allowed target. Extending the schema is needed for Active Directory backup but does not enable dual backup.

prompt: An organization runs Windows LAPS in legacy Microsoft LAPS emulation mode on its domain-joined servers. A new requirement states that local administrator passwords stored in Active Directory must be encrypted and that previous passwords must be retrievable. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Keep emulation mode and tighten the ACL on the legacy password attribute
Keep emulation mode and encrypt the domain controller disks with BitLocker
Reinstall the legacy LAPS client-side extension on the servers
Move the servers to native Windows LAPS policy settings

explanation: Password encryption and password history are features of native Windows LAPS; emulation mode stores passwords in Active Directory in clear text like the legacy product. Tightening the ACL limits who can read the attribute but the value is still unencrypted and there is no history. Reinstalling the legacy client-side extension keeps the legacy behavior and the product is deprecated. BitLocker on domain controllers protects disks at rest, not the attribute from directory readers.

prompt: An organization wants every storage account and App Service app in all subscriptions to follow its PaaS security baseline, and deployments that violate the baseline must be rejected at creation time. What should the architect specify?

options.text: An Azure Policy initiative with deny effects assigned at the management group
Read-only resource locks applied to every production resource group
A custom Azure RBAC role that removes the write permission for app settings
Defender for Cloud recommendations reviewed by resource owners every week

explanation: Azure Policy with deny effects evaluates requests in Azure Resource Manager and rejects non-compliant deployments, and assigning the initiative at a management group covers all subscriptions beneath it. Defender for Cloud recommendations report gaps after resources exist and block nothing. Read-only locks stop all changes, compliant or not, and do not evaluate configuration. A custom RBAC role controls who may act, not whether the resulting configuration meets the baseline.

prompt: A company relies on several non-Microsoft SaaS applications such as Salesforce and ServiceNow. The architect must specify how the security configuration of these applications is assessed against best practices, with findings surfaced alongside Microsoft Secure Score. What should be specified?

options.text: Cloud discovery reports generated from firewall and proxy logs
SaaS security posture management through app connectors in Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Entra application proxy published in front of each SaaS application
Foundational CSPM in Defender for Cloud with a connector for each SaaS vendor

explanation: Defender for Cloud Apps provides SaaS security posture management: app connectors read the configuration of supported SaaS apps and surface misconfiguration recommendations in Secure Score. Defender for Cloud CSPM assesses cloud infrastructure in Azure, AWS and GCP, not SaaS application settings. Cloud discovery identifies which apps are used and their risk scores, not how your tenant of the app is configured. Application proxy publishes on-premises web apps and assesses nothing.

prompt: A security baseline for IaaS states that new Azure virtual machines must be protected against bootkits and rootkits by using secure boot, a virtual TPM and boot integrity monitoring. Which requirement should the architect specify for VM deployments?

options.text: Trusted launch
Azure Dedicated Host
Encryption at host
Azure Disk Encryption

explanation: Trusted launch provides secure boot, vTPM and boot integrity monitoring for generation 2 VMs, defending against boot-level malware. Azure Disk Encryption encrypts OS and data volumes inside the guest. Encryption at host encrypts data on the VM host, including temp disks and caches. Azure Dedicated Host gives physical isolation of the server and does nothing to verify the boot chain.

prompt: Back-end services call the service APIs of an Azure IoT hub to send commands to devices. A review finds that the services use the hub's shared access policy keys stored in configuration files. Which requirement should the architect specify?

options.text: Give each back-end service its own device identity with a symmetric key
Authenticate the services with Microsoft Entra ID and Azure RBAC by using managed identities
Generate shared access signature tokens with a one-hour lifetime from the policy key
Restrict the IoT hub with an IP filter that lists the back-end service addresses

explanation: IoT Hub service APIs support Microsoft Entra authentication with Azure RBAC, and managed identities remove stored secrets while allowing granular permissions. Short-lived SAS tokens still have to be signed with the shared access policy key that is stored somewhere. An IP filter narrows the network path but leaves the shared key in use. Device identities are for devices connecting to the hub and cannot authorize service-side operations.

prompt: A factory sends telemetry to Azure IoT Hub over ExpressRoute private peering. The security requirement is that the hub must not accept device connections from the public internet at all. What should the architect specify?

options.text: A private endpoint for the IoT hub with public network access disabled
IP filter rules that allow only the factory's public IP addresses
Monthly rotation of device keys in the identity registry
A minimum TLS version of 1.2 enforced on the IoT hub

explanation: A private endpoint gives the hub a private IP reachable over ExpressRoute private peering, and disabling public network access closes the public endpoint. IP filter rules still use the public endpoint, only restricting which addresses may reach it. Enforcing TLS 1.2 protects traffic in transit but not the exposure of the endpoint. Rotating device keys limits credential lifetime and has no effect on network reachability.

prompt: A web app on Azure App Service is published through Azure Front Door Premium with a WAF policy. The architect must ensure that requests cannot bypass the WAF by calling the app's default hostname, including requests sent through Front Door profiles that belong to other customers. What should be specified?

options.text: An access restriction for the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag that also matches the profile's X-Azure-FDID header
An access restriction that allows only the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag
A custom domain and managed certificate bound to the App Service app
A CORS policy on the app that lists only the Front Door hostname

explanation: Restricting the app to the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag limits traffic to Front Door infrastructure, and filtering on the X-Azure-FDID header ensures it comes from your own profile. The service tag alone still admits traffic from any other customer's Front Door profile. CORS is enforced by browsers for cross-origin scripts and does not stop direct requests. A custom domain and certificate do not restrict who can reach the default hostname.

prompt: An architect reviews deployment practices for Azure App Service. Developers deploy by using downloaded publish profiles over FTP and the SCM site. The architect must reduce the risk of stolen deployment credentials. Which requirement should be specified?

options.text: Deploy only to a staging slot and then swap it into production
Enforce FTPS only so that the publishing credentials are encrypted in transit
Reset the publish profile every month and distribute the new file to developers
Disable basic authentication for FTP and SCM and deploy with Microsoft Entra identities

explanation: Disabling basic authentication removes the static publishing credentials, so deployments must use Microsoft Entra-backed identities that are subject to RBAC and Conditional Access. Monthly resets still leave a shared static credential in circulation. Deployment slots improve release safety but use the same publishing credentials. FTPS encrypts the session, yet the same username and password can still be stolen from developer machines and reused.

prompt: An AKS security standard states that clusters may run only container images that come from the company's own Azure Container Registry, and that pods referencing other registries must be rejected. What should the architect specify?

options.text: Azure Policy for Kubernetes with an allowed container images policy set to deny
A network security group that blocks outbound traffic to Docker Hub addresses
Defender for Containers alerts for images pulled from unknown registries
Image signing enabled on the company's Azure Container Registry

explanation: The Azure Policy add-on for AKS enforces policies at admission, and the allowed container images policy with a deny effect rejects pods whose image does not match the approved registry pattern. Defender for Containers alerts detect activity after the fact and do not block admission. Blocking Docker Hub addresses in an NSG is brittle and leaves every other registry reachable. Signing images in your registry does not prevent unsigned images from other registries unless an admission control verifies it.

prompt: An AKS cluster must pull images from a private Azure Container Registry. The standard forbids registry passwords or tokens stored in the cluster. How should the architect specify registry authentication?

options.text: Enable the registry admin user and reference it in an image pull secret
Enable anonymous pull on the registry and restrict it by IP address
Create a repository-scoped token and store it in a ConfigMap
Grant the AcrPull role on the registry to the cluster's kubelet managed identity

explanation: Attaching the registry by granting AcrPull to the kubelet managed identity lets nodes pull images with Microsoft Entra authentication and no stored secret. The registry admin user is a shared password account that would have to be stored in a pull secret. Anonymous pull removes authentication altogether. A repository-scoped token is still a secret, and a ConfigMap stores it in plain text in the cluster.

prompt: A platform team wants Kubernetes deployments to be audited or blocked when the image has vulnerability findings that violate the organization's vulnerability policy. Which capability should the architect specify?

options.text: Gated deployment rules in Defender for Containers
Kubernetes network policies in every namespace
Geo-replication of the Azure Container Registry
Binary drift detection in Defender for Containers

explanation: Gated deployment in Defender for Containers uses the vulnerability assessment findings associated with an image to audit or block its deployment to Kubernetes. Binary drift detection concerns processes started at runtime that were not in the original image. Network policies restrict pod traffic and know nothing about image vulnerabilities. Geo-replication improves registry availability and has no security gating function.

prompt: The SOC wants to be alerted, and optionally to block, when a process starts inside a running container from an executable that was not part of the original container image. Which capability should the architect specify?

options.text: Agentless discovery for Kubernetes
Gated deployment rules in Defender for Containers
Registry image vulnerability assessment
Binary drift detection in Defender for Containers

explanation: Binary drift detection is a sensor-based Defender for Containers capability that detects, and with drift policies can block, external processes that did not originate from the container image. Gated deployment acts at admission time on image vulnerability findings, before a container runs. Agentless discovery inventories clusters and configurations through the API. Registry vulnerability assessment scans stored images and cannot see runtime process activity.

prompt: A security requirement states that the Kubernetes API server of a new AKS cluster must have no public IP address and must be reachable only from the hub network and peered networks. Which cluster design should the architect specify?

options.text: A public cluster with Kubernetes network policies
A public cluster with API server authorized IP ranges
A private AKS cluster
A public cluster behind an Azure Firewall DNAT rule

explanation: In a private AKS cluster the API server is exposed only through a private address inside the virtual network, so it has no public endpoint. Authorized IP ranges restrict who can reach the API server, but it still has a public IP. Kubernetes network policies control pod traffic and not access to the control plane. A DNAT rule on Azure Firewall would publish something to the internet rather than remove the public endpoint.

prompt: An audit finds that AKS administrators share a kubeconfig file containing a client certificate with cluster-admin rights. The architect must make cluster access attributable to individual users and subject to Conditional Access. What should be specified?

options.text: A separate client certificate issued to each administrator from the cluster CA
Microsoft Entra integration for the cluster with local accounts disabled
A shared Kubernetes service account token rotated every week
SSH access to the nodes restricted to a jump server

explanation: Integrating AKS with Microsoft Entra ID makes administrators authenticate as themselves, so Conditional Access and group-based RBAC apply, and disabling local accounts removes the shared certificate path. Per-admin certificates from the cluster CA improve attribution but cannot be revoked easily or governed by Conditional Access. A shared service account token is still a shared, non-attributable credential. Restricting node SSH does not address API server authentication.

prompt: Pods in an AKS cluster must read secrets from Azure Key Vault. Each application must have its own least-privilege identity, and no credential may be stored in the cluster. Which design should the architect specify?
